### 41f. Where Axis 1 actually sits

**Challenge 3 does not fix what I claimed.** An unknown worker makes doubt structural, repairing F2's fatal
weakness — **but payoffs remain separable**, so a stranger on task 1 independent of task 2 is a harder
assignment problem, not a coordination one. **It solves the doubt problem and leaves the collapse in place.**
After 1+2, not instead of it.

---

## 42. Identifiability measured — 2.65 overall, 1.60 for the pair that matters

_The reviewer corrected the test before it ran: **"is the worker stable?" is the wrong question.** PLASTIC does
not need determinism, it needs behaviour **more likely under one type than another** — a distributional
condition. So the criterion is a **ratio**, and the matched-cell variance that alarmed me measures only the
**denominator**. Large within-worker variance is compatible with perfect separability._

```
identifiable  iff  BETWEEN-worker variance  >  WITHIN-worker variance
```

**Computed on the existing corpus with the committed reader — 4 agents, 213 (run × agent) signatures, 9 tools,
zero new runs.** Signature = normalised tool-name distribution per run; distance = total variation.

```
mean WITHIN-worker  TV distance = 0.239
mean BETWEEN-worker TV distance = 0.633
RATIO = 2.65
```

**So identifiability is NOT ruled out** — workers are distinguishable by tool-use signature despite large
run-to-run variance, exactly as the reviewer predicted. **But the pairwise breakdown is where the finding is:**

| ratio | pair | between | within |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1.60** | **`portfolio_analyst` / `risk_analyst`** | 0.447 | 0.280 |
| 1.83 | `portfolio_analyst` / `screening_analyst` | 0.511 | 0.279 |
| 2.52 | `risk_analyst` / `screening_analyst` | 0.698 | 0.277 |
| 3.43–3.70 | anything / `audit_coordinator` | 0.697–0.748 | 0.20 |

> **The least identifiable pair — 1.60, barely above parity — is the SUBSTITUTE PAIR**, the two workers holding
> identical capability lists, and **precisely the pair the manager must discriminate between in order to
> reroute.** Identifiability holds in general and is weakest exactly where the research question needs it.

**That is the capability-versus-policy root showing up as a number.** The substitutes are near-indistinguishable
**behaviourally as well as declaratively** — so they are not merely interchangeable by capability lookup, they
have **no distinct behavioural signature to be matched.** A PLASTIC-style mechanism has nothing to grip on
exactly where we have been asking the manager to choose.

**And `audit_coordinator` is the counter-example that makes the reading credible:** within-worker variance 0.126,
half the analysts', and every pairing with it exceeds 3.4. **A worker with a narrow, distinctive role does have a
signature.** So the low ratios are a property of the substitute design, not an artifact of LLM noise.

### 42a. What this check can and cannot conclude — pre-committed before it ran

**It can DISQUALIFY and cannot QUALIFY.** It measures workers **as currently configured** — capability-shaped,
with no policy dimension in the scenario — so a sequencing or scoping sensitivity **that does not yet exist
cannot be measured on runs where nothing depended on it.** **Treat 2.65 as "not ruled out", never as
"established".**

### 42b. The pre-commitment that keeps a low number from reading as a kill

**"Instability is the phenomenon" is coherent in exactly one form.** Pure unpredictability does not rescue a
formulation, it **kills** it: if observing a teammate does not reduce uncertainty about its future behaviour,
there is nothing to adapt on and the best policy is a fixed robust one. **Adaptation requires observation to be
informative.**

> **The version that works is PARTIAL IDENTIFIABILITY: the teammate is unpredictable in some dimensions and
> predictable in others, and the manager's problem is DISCOVERING WHICH DIMENSION IS WORTH MODELLING.**

**That survives the flaky-API test** — a flaky API has no dimensions to discriminate between — and **a low ratio
points TOWARD it rather than away.** Pre-committed before the numbers were computed, so that a bad result would
relocate the programme rather than end it. **And 1.60 on the substitute pair against 3.70 on
`audit_coordinator` is exactly the partial-identifiability signature: predictable in role, unpredictable within
a role-equivalence class.**

---

## 43. The substitute pair is indiscriminable on every statistic the reader can see

_The reviewer's objection to §42 was that the statistic was **under-powered by construction**: the substitutes
hold the **same toolset** (both `robust` tier, same nine tools), so a marginal over tool NAMES has almost nothing
to separate — 1.60 was partly determined before any data was read. The rerun was framed not as a check but as **a
decision between two designs**. It decided._

| statistic | substitute-pair ratio | rank among all pairs |
|---|---|---|
| tool-name marginal | **1.60** | lowest of 6 |
| parameterisation (`column='all'` vs per-column, dataset, batch) | **1.76** | lowest of 6 |
| **sequence bigrams** — AATEAM's actual claim | **1.30** | lowest of 6 |

> **Three statistics, three times the least discriminable pair in the team.** Parameterisation added a little
> signal (1.60 → 1.76) and did not change the ordering or approach the `audit_coordinator` range (3.2–3.4). **The
> substitutes are indiscriminable on everything the reader can see.**

### 43a. And the trajectory statistic is the WORST, which is a finding about applying AHT to LLM agents

**AATEAM's contribution is that types are separable over trajectories rather than in aggregate.** Here the
trajectory statistic performs **worse than the aggregate one** — and the reason is in the denominator:

```
within-worker variance      tool-name 0.24   parameterisation 0.29   SEQUENCE 0.58
between-worker separation   tool-name 0.63   parameterisation 0.68   sequence 0.88
```

**Sequence separation rises (0.63 → 0.88) but within-worker sequence variance rises FASTER (0.24 → 0.58).** An
LLM worker's *ordering* is far less stable run-to-run than *what tools it reaches for at all.*

> **Measured here: sequence variance rises FASTER than sequence separation** (0.24→0.58 against 0.63→0.88), so
> **in this corpus** trajectory-based type identification is **less viable than aggregate matching.** The
> mechanism that would make it general — sampling perturbs ordering more readily than tool selection — is
> **plausible and is a hypothesis doing the generalising, not the measurement.** _Scoped on the reviewer's
> objection: stated as a property of LLM workers, the first reviewer with a different scenario produces a
> counterexample; stated as measured-here-with-a-mechanism, it survives._ One scenario, four agents, one model —
> **and it would not have been found by testing one statistic.**

### 43b. What the ratio does NOT measure, and nobody has specified the other half

**The ratio measures DISCRIMINABILITY, not USEFULNESS.** A signature that separates two workers but predicts
nothing about the quality of their output is **real and inert**. Any formulation needs the signature to be
**predictive of something the manager acts on**, and **passing the discriminability check does not deliver
that.** The second half of this check is unspecified.

### 43c. The design the result forces

**"Identical capabilities, different policies" fails the flaky-API test in its generic form.** Two workers with
identical capabilities and different **failure profiles** are **two flaky APIs with different defect rates** —
observe outputs, learn the rates, allocate. Reaction suffices; no teammate required.

**The version that passes is narrower:**

| generic policy difference | worker A errs at rate p, B at rate q | **two flaky APIs** |
|---|---|---|
| **instruction-responsiveness** | **the SAME task description produces different behaviour in A and B, and the manager must discover which framing works for which** | **teammate modelling** |

> **An API does not respond differently to how you phrase the request. A teammate does.** So
> **instruction-responsiveness** is what converts the substitute pair from the thing that breaks every mechanism
> into the thing the study is about — and it is Challenge 4's condition arriving from the other direction:
> **AHT iff the manager must DISCOVER which instruction works for this particular worker.**

**`refine_task` is the lever for the same reason it was Challenge 4's lever.** The manager's problem becomes
genuinely non-lookup: **the right INSTRUCTION depends on the worker, not just the right ASSIGNMENT.** Capability
lookup gives nothing; output observation gives a rate; **only interaction gives the mapping.**

### 43d. The manufacturing risk, stated rather than buried

**Engineering two workers to respond differently to the same instruction is manufacturing the phenomenon**, and
the researcher has warned against solving problems we created. **The defence has to be made explicitly:** the
manipulation is on the worker's **system prompt** — the same lever `MODEL_PROMPT_JUDGMENT` already uses and which
was accepted — and the phenomenon is not exotic, since two people with the same job title respond differently to
the same brief.

> **What would make it indefensible is engineering THE DIFFERENCE THE MANAGER NEEDS TO FIND — building in the
> answer.** What keeps it honest is making the workers differ in a way **we do not tune to be discoverable**, and
> measuring whether the manager finds it. **That distinction is the one to hold when this is specified.**

---

## 44. The pre-commitment protocol for an instruction-responsiveness design

_My proposed guard — *"specify the difference by its cause, not its signature, before knowing what the manager
would need to notice"* — had **three gaps.** Two became tests; the third is a limit on the rule's reach._

### 44a. GAP 1 — it constrained each attempt, not the SEQUENCE of attempts

Write a disposition pair by cause, measure discoverability, get nothing. Write a second. A third. **Every
individual attempt satisfies the rule, and the selection among them is by discoverability — so the manufacturing
moves into the retry loop, where the rule cannot see it.** Garden of forking paths, and the same shape as the
prompt-wording work already halted: each candidate defensible, the search over candidates not.

> **Bound the attempts in advance, as payload fixes were bounded at three. ONE disposition pair, specified
> before running, reported whatever it yields.** A second pair is a **second experiment with its own
> pre-commitment**, reported *alongside* the first rather than replacing it.

**Otherwise *"if it turns out undiscoverable, that is a result"* is a disposition we would be relying on
ourselves to honour at the moment it costs most.**

### 44b. GAP 2 — cause and signature do not separate for PROMPT manipulations

In the toolset lever, cause (tool swapped) and signature (method reported) are genuinely different levels and the
rule bites. **In a prompt manipulation the behaviour is written directly** — *"asks for clarification when a
brief is ambiguous"* is **simultaneously the cause and a near-verbatim description of what the manager will
observe.** The levels collapse and the rule stops constraining.

> **The checkable form: THE SPECIFIED CAUSE MUST NOT NAME AN OBSERVABLE THE MANAGER RECEIVES.**

**A grep against the observation surface, not a judgement about intent. The surface, verified:**

```
workflow_summary: str            available_agent_metadata: list[AgentConfig]
recent_messages: list[Message]   <- rendered at structured_manager.py:274
task_status_counts, *_task_ids   constraints, stakeholder_profile
```

| *"asks for clarification when a brief is ambiguous"* | **FAILS.** `recent_messages` is manager-visible and rendered, so **clarification requests are read off directly** — the signature has been handed over |
|---|---|
| *"cautious about extrapolating beyond available data"* | **PASSES.** Its behavioural expression is indirect; the manager must **infer** it from what the worker does |

### 44c. GAP 3 — the discoverability check must be MECHANICAL

**If we inspect traces looking for the difference we wrote, we will find it** — the §6h pattern at the *analysis*
layer rather than the scenario layer. **The check must be the ratio machinery from §42–43**, over the same three
statistics, **with no hand-inspection permitted before the number lands.** Cheap, since it exists, and it removes
us from the loop **at the point where our knowledge is most contaminating.**

### 44d. The limit that stays open

**Discriminability is not usefulness.** A signature that separates two workers and predicts nothing about their
output is real and inert. **Left named and unresolved rather than given an invented second-half criterion** —
what the manager would act on depends on which formulation survives, and specifying it now would be **fitting the
test to a design that does not exist.**

---

## 45. NEW FORMULATION — the manager as CONVENTION-KEEPER

_New idea for this pass. **"Ad hoc teamwork" originally means teams assembled WITHOUT PRIOR COORDINATION, and the
classic object in that literature is CONVENTIONS** — arbitrary-but-shared choices that make joint work
interoperable. **We have never considered conventions.** Every formulation so far has been about competence,
quality, or capability._

### 45a. The formulation

**A team develops implicit conventions:** which format, which units, which ordering, what counts as reported,
what "done" looks like. **These are arbitrary — several choices are equally good — but they must be SHARED.** A
newcomer, or a worker whose disposition shifts, does not share them. **The resulting failure is a coordination
failure arising from DIFFERENCE, not deficiency.**

**In manager-agent terms:** the manager's unique lever is that it can make an implicit convention **explicit in a
task description** (`refine_task`). **Adaptation = converting tacit team knowledge into explicit instruction.**

### 45b. Why it is structurally the manager's problem — the role argument we have been missing

> **The manager is the ONLY party that sees multiple workers' outputs.** A worker sees artifacts but holds no
> mandate over anyone else's representation. **So noticing and repairing a convention mismatch is STRUCTURALLY
> the coordinator's job** — not an arbitrary assignment of the task to it.

Every previous formulation had to argue the manager *should* do something. **This one derives the manager's role
from its position in the information structure**, which is the kind of argument the Manager Agent formulation
supports and that we have not previously produced.

### 45c. It passes the gates, including the two that killed everything else

| **flaky-API test** | **PASSES.** An API has **no conventions** — conventions exist because agents coordinate. Decisively: **you cannot TELL an API to adopt a convention; you can tell an agent.** The manager's lever only functions on a teammate |
|---|---|
| **difference not deficiency** (§40c) | **PASSES by construction** — a convention is arbitrary, so a mismatch is not an error |
| **non-separability** (§40b) | **PASSES** — a convention is a **joint** property; one worker's representation is right only relative to the others' |
| **capability vs policy** (§41d) | **PASSES** — which convention a worker follows is a **policy** property, invisible in a capability list |

### 45d. Small test — the substrate exists, and the result is CONFOUNDED

**Test: do workers differ systematically in HOW they report, holding WHAT constant?** Distinct artifacts,
representational features only:

```
worker              N     per-column   cutoffs inline   explicit total   cites formula
audit_coordinator   434       2%             0%              0%               3%
portfolio_analyst   341      29%            25%             19%              25%
risk_analyst        149      25%            15%             15%               0%
screening_analyst   324      42%            35%             33%              46%
```

**Representational choice varies enormously — 2% to 42% on the same feature — so conventions are a real, varying
dimension in this corpus.** That is the substrate the formulation needs.

> **But the result is CONFOUNDED and must not be cited as evidence.** The workers hold different task mixes, and
> `cites formula` matches the **mean+2·SD** formula — which `portfolio_analyst` reaches only **after the
> perturbation** and `risk_analyst` never has reason to use. **So the 25%-versus-0% gap is task allocation and
> the perturbation, not convention.** A matched-task comparison is required, exactly as RE's matched-cell
> requirement was. **Hypothesis-generating, not evidence.**

**And a near-miss worth recording:** the substitute pair is **indiscriminable on tool use** (1.60 / 1.76 / 1.30,
§43) while **apparently differing on representation** (25% vs 15% cutoffs-inline). If that survives task
matching, **the substitutes are discriminable in CONVENTION while indiscriminable in BEHAVIOUR** — which would
make convention the identifying dimension that tool-use statistics cannot see.

### 45e. Four challenges against it, raised before the reviewer does

| **1. Is it just schema validation?** | If the convention is **machine-checkable** (units, format), noticing a mismatch is validation, not AHT. **It is AHT only if the convention is genuinely ARBITRARY (several equally good options) and TACIT (written nowhere).** A design constraint, not a detail |
|---|---|
| **2. Does the manager have to INFER it?** | If the task description specifies the format, there is no convention — only a requirement. **So the design needs UNDER-SPECIFIED tasks** — and under-specification is exactly what our method-requirement setup was built to avoid. **Probably the hardest tension** |
| **3. Does it collapse to "the manager writes better specs"?** | That is requirements engineering. **Escape: it is AHT iff WHICH convention to adopt depends on what the INCUMBENT TEAM already does** — adapt the newcomer to the team, not to a global standard. If a global standard exists, the problem dissolves |
| **4. Scoring without ground truth?** | **Internal consistency across the team's artifacts** — the same joint-property logic as §36b, needing no oracle because the property is internal to the outputs |

### 45f. A second candidate, noted not developed

**Scheduling under scope-dependent behaviour.** Workers compete for timesteps and a shared budget, so payoffs
become non-separable **through resource contention** rather than output comparability. Scheduling well requires
predicting **how long each worker takes and how it degrades under larger scope** — the *"capable but slow"* /
*"degrades on large batches"* dimension. **The bandit objection:** a bandit arm has no policy, so this is AHT
only if **the worker's behaviour depends on HOW the manager scopes the work**, making the arm's distribution a
function of how it is pulled — teammate modelling rather than parameter estimation.

---

## 46. Convention-keeper survives its challenges — and hits a rule

### 46a. Challenge 2 dissolves: CONTENT is specified, FORM is not

**The reviewer's resolution, and it needs no change to the scenario.** The task says:

> *"Report the sum of the four flagged counts as the metric, **with method and cutoffs in details**."*

**That specifies WHAT must appear — a method, the cutoffs, a total. It says nothing about HOW:** inline or
per-column, one line or four, formula cited or not.

```
CONTENT   specified and fully measurable   does the artifact name the right method?
FORM      entirely unspecified             in what representation?          <- the convention
```

> **Under-specification and measurability are not competing for the same slot — they are on different axes.**
> §45's table is a measurement of the second *under* the first, which is why the variation was 2%–42% while the
> requirement stayed checkable.

### 46b. And one distinction carries challenges 1 and 3 as well

> **Validation compares an artifact to a SPEC. Convention-keeping compares it to PEERS.**

**Challenge 1 (is it schema validation?): no** — a schema needs a standard, and there is none for form. **The only
referent for "right form" is what the rest of the team does. Challenge 3 (does it collapse to writing better
specs?): only if a global standard exists, and it does not** — which convention is correct is defined by the
incumbent team. **That was the proposed escape and it holds.**

### 46c. The objection I did not make, and it is the real one

> **A convention only matters if something downstream BREAKS when it is violated.** A convention with no
> sensitive consumer is a **stylistic difference**, not a coordination failure — and engineering the consumer to
> break is manufacturing.

**In this scenario, mostly nothing breaks.** Reconciliation runs through `analyze_audit_artifacts`, a **tool**,
which parses robustly and is **format-insensitive**.

**The reviewer's answer is that a format-SENSITIVE consumer already exists, unengineered — some reconciliations
are performed by READING both artifacts rather than by calling the tool. Verified, and it is THIN:**

```
"reading both native artifacts"   8 files, ~5 distinct runs of 54     READING -- format-SENSITIVE
analyze_audit_artifacts           305 files                           TOOL    -- format-insensitive
```

**A looser pattern inflates this to 45 runs and inverts the conclusion — and it is the §6f failure again, mine
this time.** A second check using `computed? the absolute difference` alongside the reading phrases returned **45
of 54 runs**, which reads as *"the reading route is the norm"*. **The examples show why it is wrong:**

> *"**The reconcile TOOL computed** the absolute difference between the Batch A Robust Audit (89 flagged items)
> and the Batch A Rapid Screen (59 flagged items)"*

**The pattern matched TOOL-route reconciliations described in prose.** *"Computed the absolute difference"* is what
the tool does, narrated. **So the loose check measured the wrong subject and would have supported the opposite
finding — a check satisfied by the wrong subject, for the fourth time in this project and the second by me.** The
narrow phrase (`"reading both native artifacts"`, ~5 runs) is the accurate measure; **the broad check confirms the
rarity rather than contradicting it, but only once the matches are read rather than counted.**

**So the natural sensitivity is real but rare.** The convention has teeth in a **minority** of runs, which means a
study would need the reading route to be the **norm** rather than the exception.

### 46d. And making it the norm collides with the core-tools rule

**`CLAUDE.md`: never disable an agent's CORE tools.** So the reading route **cannot** be forced by removing
`analyze_audit_artifacts` from the reconciler — that switches the worker off rather than grading it, which is the
prohibited move.

> **The remaining route is to make the TASK require something the tool cannot do**, so reading is the only way to
> satisfy it while every tool stays in place. **That is a scenario-design question and it is unresolved** — and it
> is the first constraint this formulation has hit that is a project rule rather than an argument.

### 46e. The closure: the extraction saga IS this problem, from the analysis side

**Five surface forms for one cutoff. RE's regex missed the screens; the reviewer's missed the control robusts.
Both drew wrong conclusions from a format divergence in artifacts produced by ONE worker model under ONE
prompt.**

> **We were the downstream consumer that could not parse divergent representations, and it cost this project
> hours and two false findings.** That is the strongest available argument that the phenomenon is real and
> consequential rather than stylistic — **and it is evidence we generated by accident, on ourselves, before the
> formulation existed.**

**Convention beats the scheduling candidate**, for the reason in §45b rather than any mechanism: **it is the only
formulation in this project whose role argument is DERIVED.** Scheduling would have to argue the manager *should*
do it.

---

## 47. Convention-keeper: the teeth problem solved, and the closure holds for a principled reason

### 47a. Route choice is an ASSIGNMENT ARTEFACT, not a signature — check not run

**Proposed check (is the reconciliation route a per-worker behavioural signature?): dropped before running.**

```
reconciliation, by producer:
  audit_coordinator   41   tool route     -- HAS analyze_audit_artifacts (coordination tier)
  portfolio_analyst    1   READING route  -- does NOT have it (robust tier)
```

> **The reading route is not a worker choosing a format-sensitive method over a robust one. It is a worker that
> LACKS THE TOOL being handed the task and having to read.** The route is determined by **who got the task**, so
> the check would have measured **the manager's allocation, not the worker's disposition.**

**Recorded as a check correctly abandoned** — the fifth time a proposed measurement in this project would have
had the wrong subject, and the first caught *before* it ran.

### 47b. And that solves the constraint §46d could not argue past

**Two ways to make reading the norm, neither of which removes a tool from anyone:**

| 1 | assign reconciliation to a worker whose toolset does not cover it | **OBSERVED** in the corpus — but manager-dependent |
|---|---|---|
| **2** | **design a comparison the tool does not implement** | **deterministic; the remaining route from §46d** |

> **Neither is the prohibited move.** `CLAUDE.md` forbids **taking a core tool away from an agent.** It does not
> require every task to be satisfiable by its assignee's toolset — **a workflow containing a task no single tool
> covers is ordinary design, not a disabled worker.** Every agent keeps everything it has and still must read.

**Route 2 is the one, because route 1 depends on the manager misassigning** — which makes the sensitivity a
consequence of an allocation error rather than a property of the task.

### 47c. The closure survives — and my objection was wrong about WHY the tool succeeded

**I assumed `analyze_audit_artifacts` was a ROBUST parser and our regexes were brittle ones. Verified false:**

```
analyze_audit_artifacts -> artifact_metric(name) -> extract_metric(resource.content)
                           reads the CONSTRAINED `metric:` value
we were parsing            the OPEN `details:` prose, where the cutoffs live
```

> **The tool is not robust to representational variation. It is INSENSITIVE to it, because it does not consume
> the representation at all.**

**And a better parser is impossible in principle here — we proved that ourselves.** RE derived surface shapes
**from the corpus** (the correct method, not a pattern written from one example) and the reader **still failed on
run 19 with two forms nobody had seen.** Our own recorded rule: *deriving from a corpus is a bet that the next
sample lies inside the observed support, and for LLM-generated prose the distribution is not closed.*

> **So the phenomenon is NOT "brittle parsers break on heterogeneous output", which a better parser fixes. It is:
> AN OPEN-ENDED CHANNEL CANNOT BE MADE SAFE ON THE CONSUMER SIDE, BECAUSE AN OPEN SET CANNOT BE ENUMERATED.**
> The only remaining lever is **the producer** — which is convention-keeping.

**And the flaky-API test confirms the direction rather than merely permitting it:** you can write a more tolerant
parser for an API; **you cannot ask an API to adopt a convention.** The producer-side fix exists *only because the
producer is an agent.*

### 47d. The scope the claim must carry

**My objection landed partially, so the claim is narrowed:** representational divergence is consequential **for
consumers of OPEN channels**, and **structured channels sidestep it entirely** — which is exactly why the tool was
unaffected across 305 files.

> **Scope: agent-to-agent communication in natural language — which is most of it — and NOT anything a schema
> already constrains.** Smaller than *"conventions matter"*, and the version the evidence supports.

### 47e. Status of the formulation after two passes

| role argument | **derived**, not assigned — the manager is the only party seeing multiple workers' outputs (§45b) |
|---|---|
| four challenges | **all resolved** — content/form axes (§46a), validation-vs-peers (§46b) |
| the teeth problem | **solved without violating the core-tools rule** — route 2 (§47b) |
| the closure argument | **holds, on the open-set impossibility** rather than on parser quality (§47c) |
| scope | **stated and narrowed** — open natural-language channels only (§47d) |
| **still open** | whether representational divergence is **per-worker stable** at all, which needs matched tasks (§45d) — and the discriminability-vs-usefulness gap (§43b) |

---

## 48. Convention-keeper is DEAD as stated — workers hold no stable representation

_The reviewer produced the number I said could kill it, and proposed the discriminating check. **I ran it. It
kills the formulation's central object.** Matched task, so allocation and perturbation are held fixed._

```
task                            worker              n    DISTINCT SHAPES   modal share
Batch A Robust Audit            portfolio_analyst   61        38              10%
Batch A Robust Audit            risk_analyst        24        11              33%
Batch A Rapid Screen            screening_analyst   83        31              17%
Batch A/B/C Method Reconcil.    audit_coordinator   83/79/82   4/5/4        93/95/95%
```

> **On a matched task, one worker produces 38 distinct representational shapes across 61 artifacts, with the
> modal form holding 10%.** There is **no stable per-worker representation** here. **And if a worker does not hold
> a representation stably, it has no convention to share, none to violate, and nothing for a newcomer to fail to
> match.** The formulation's central object does not exist in this corpus.

**§45d's 2%–42% "between-worker" variation is at least partly this same within-worker churn showing through an
unmatched comparison.** The confound I flagged there was worse than I thought: not only task mix, but the fact
that **there was no stable per-worker value for the unmatched comparison to be confounding.**

### 48a. And this is the extraction saga, measured rather than suffered

**The five-to-seven surface forms that broke the reviewer's regex, RE's regex, and RE's corpus-derived shape
survey were not a fleet of differently-conventioned workers. They were ONE worker, on ONE task, varying run to
run.** The reviewer offered the saga as the closure argument reading it as divergence *between* producers; it is
divergence *within* one. **Neither of us saw that until the matched comparison was run.**

### 48b. The reviewer's escape hatch — and the confound that weakens it

**Their prediction: if `audit_coordinator` is also multi-shape, the finding is general and the formulation is
dead; if single-shape, stability varies by ROLE and the formulation survives narrowly.** It came back
**single-shape — 93–95% modal.** But:

> **`audit_coordinator`'s modal shape is `<none>` — meaning NONE of the structural features fire.** Its
> reconciliation output is a single difference value with no cutoffs, columns or formulas to arrange. **So its
> apparent stability may be LOW REPRESENTATIONAL AFFORDANCE rather than a held convention** — a short output has
> fewer degrees of freedom to vary in.

**So "stability varies by role" is not established. The alternative — stability tracks OUTPUT COMPLEXITY — fits
the same data**, and the two are not separated by anything measured here. `audit_coordinator` also had the lowest
within-worker *tool* variance (0.126, §42), which is consistent with either reading.

### 48c. What survives, and it is not nothing

| the **role argument** | **untouched.** The manager is still the only party seeing multiple workers' outputs; that derivation never depended on the phenomenon existing (§45b) |
|---|---|
| the **closure argument** | **stronger, and harder.** An open channel cannot be made safe consumer-side (§47c) **and the producer side is not stable either** — so convention-keeping would have to **CREATE** stability rather than exploit it. A more demanding engineering claim, honestly stated |
| the **scope restriction** | **now doing real work.** The finding is: **LLM workers under a fixed prompt do not spontaneously hold representational conventions.** Not *"conventions do not matter"* — **"conventions are not free"**, which is the more useful claim and the one this corpus supports |

### 48d. Recorded disposition

**DEAD as stated.** Convention-keeping presupposed a convention to keep. **The measured fact is the opposite of
its premise**, and the honest form of what remains is a **negative result about LLM workers plus an unresolved
confound** — not a formulation. **Two passes, one derived role argument kept, central object falsified by a free
query on the existing corpus.**

---

## 49. The substrate claim is UNTESTED, not answered — and §43 measured an uninformative population

_I proposed that two formulations dying of *"within-worker variance swamps between-worker structure"* pointed to a
substrate property of LLM workers. **The reviewer refused it: two instances sharing a STATISTIC, not a CAUSE.**_

```
§43   substitute pair near parity on tool use     cause: WE GAVE THEM IDENTICAL TOOLSETS   -> SCENARIO DESIGN
§48   38 shapes in 61 artifacts, one task         cause: FREE-FORM PROSE IS HIGH-ENTROPY   -> CHANNEL PROPERTY
```

**Neither is evidence about substrate.** The first says two workers built identical are indistinguishable — which
is what *identical* means. The second says unconstrained generation varies — true of any generative model on any
open channel.

**And my counter-evidence does not rescue it either.** `audit_coordinator` at 3.4–3.7 with within-variance 0.126
looked like proof that LLM workers *can* carry stable signatures. **Verified — it is capability-driven:**

```
COORDINATOR_TOOL_IDS = (*CORE_TOOL_IDS, "analyze_audit_artifacts")     <- ONLY the coordinator holds it
ROBUST_TOOL_IDS      = (*SHARED_TOOL_IDS, "flag_outliers_percentile")
SCREENING_TOOL_IDS   = (*SHARED_TOOL_IDS, "flag_outliers_zscore")
```

**Calling a tool only you have is a CAPABILITY signature, not a policy one.**

### 49a. And it is worse than the reviewer said — the substitutes share a PROMPT too

**Verified: `scenario.py:38-47` is a single shared worker prompt** — *"You are a loan-portfolio data analyst…"* —
used by every analyst. So `portfolio_analyst` and `risk_analyst` are identical in **tier** *and* **system prompt**.
**Nothing distinguishes them except which tasks the manager assigns.**

> **No policy difference has ever existed in this scenario, so no statistic could have found one.** Tool-name
> marginals, parameterisation and sequence bigrams all measured a population that is **identical in policy by
> construction.** **Three statistics, one uninformative population.**

**§43's 1.60 / 1.76 / 1.30 is therefore not evidence about LLM workers. It is evidence that identical things are
identical** — and it should be cited that way, not as an identifiability result.

### 49b. Every channel measured was either capability-bearing or unconstrained

```
tools, parameterisation, sequence   encode CAPABILITY -- and the substitutes are identical there by design
free-form prose (details:)          UNCONSTRAINED    -- anything varies
```

> **Nobody has measured a channel that is CONSTRAINED enough to be stable AND POLICY-BEARING rather than
> capability-bearing — because the scenario contains no policy to bear.** The substrate question is **untested**,
> not answered.

### 49c. Which makes instruction-responsiveness the DECISIVE experiment rather than one candidate among others

**Two workers, identical capability, differing in how they respond to the same instruction — then the same ratio
on the same three statistics.**

| workers built to differ are **still indiscriminable** | **the substrate claim is established**, and it rules out Axis 1 and Axis 2 mechanisms **wholesale** — the most important negative result this project could produce |
|---|---|
| they **are** discriminable | **both dead formulations died of scenario design**, not substrate, and the axes are **open** |

**One measurement, and it answers what two passes have circled.**

### 49d. The pair of negatives worth carrying regardless of which way it goes

| **conventions are not free** | LLM workers under a fixed prompt do not spontaneously hold representational conventions (§48) |
|---|---|
| **behaviour varies without converging** | **CORRECTED — my "do not spontaneously differentiate" was wrong.** They differentiate **enormously** (38 shapes / 61 artifacts, §48); what they do not do is differentiate **PERSISTENTLY.** The claim is **high within-agent variance and no stable signature — UNSTABLE HETEROGENEITY, not homogeneity** |

**Same shape, both about what you get FOR FREE rather than what is possible** — a more defensible pair than either
formulation would have been.

### 49e. The methodological tally from this pass

**The matched version of a comparison inverted its conclusion for the fourth time this session** — the reviewer
offered the extraction saga as divergence *between* producers and it was divergence *within* one, and neither of us
saw it until a matched comparison ran. **Both of us had built on the other reading.**

### 49f. Why the correction matters more than the wording

**Homogeneity would be a SCENARIO problem — we built the workers identical. Instability is a SUBSTRATE property,
and it is the one that would transfer.** And it is **precisely what breaks type identification:** PLASTIC, AATEAM,
HBA and ConvCPD all need a **signature to match**, and a signature that changes run to run cannot be matched.

**But it does not rule out Axis 2 wholesale, and the distinction is worth keeping.** **ODITS drops discrete types
entirely** — a continuous latent teammate variable tracked online, where behaviour change appears as **drift**
rather than as a switch between stored types. **Unstable heterogeneity is a problem for DISCRETE-TYPE matching and
not obviously for continuous-latent tracking**, which never assumed a stable type in the first place. So the
negative result, if it holds, rules out the **library-and-match** family and leaves the **latent-drift** family
standing.

### 49g. The routing finding: the shared prompt is the CONTROL, not the confound

**My worry was wrong and inverted.** Two workers identical in tier, prompt and capability list, differing in **one
edited field**, routing switching **3 of 3 against 0 of 37** — **that is the cleanest single-variable manipulation
in this project.** Had they differed in prompt or toolset, the switch would have been attributable to those
differences. **Because they are identical, the declaration is the only thing that could have moved it.**

> **What it cannot support, and never did: that the manager selected a BETTER worker. It selected a
> DIFFERENTLY-LABELLED one.** And since the alternative is identical-but-undegraded, **`silent_declared`'s
> 0.879–0.888 is attributable to the degraded worker NOT DOING THE ROBUST AUDITS**, not to `risk_analyst` being
> superior. **"Routing improved" invites the reading that the manager found the better analyst — there was no
> better analyst to find.**

**The genuine limitation is the one already everywhere else:** we have never tested whether the manager can choose
between workers that differ **in fact** rather than **in label.** Same gap, not a new one.

### 49h. The disposition of the pair, named in advance

**It is a contribution, of a specific and modest shape: a PRECONDITION RESULT.** A literature assumes teammates
have identifiable types; that assumption has **never been checked on LLM agents**; checking it says **the structure
is not there for free.** Worth publishing, and it is what should have been measured **before** anyone applied AHT
to LLM teams.

**What it is NOT: a mechanism.** It tells a builder what they must **install**, not how to **adapt**. **A real paper
and a small one — and calling it that now is better than discovering it at review.** Scope guard: **one model, one
prompt, one task family**, with the mechanism (sampling over an unconstrained channel produces non-repeating
surface forms) **doing the generalising as a hypothesis.**

---

## 50. Latent-drift is a MECHANISM FAMILY, not a formulation — and the negative result promotes it

_Closing the question raised at the end of §49. **My instinct was right and the reason is cleaner than the
instinct.**_

**Run the flaky-API test on it directly.** Track a continuous latent per worker, condition assignment on it. **A
flaky API has a drifting defect rate — you would track it and route accordingly, and the design is unchanged.**
So ODITS-for-a-manager, *as a formulation*, is **quality control with a filter attached.** It inherits
separability, because **tracking a drifting parameter still only tells you WHO to assign.**

> **But that is a statement about what it is FOR, not about whether it is useful.** It answers *how do you track a
> changing teammate*, and **it inherits whatever formulation it is plugged into.** Plugged into allocation: QC.
> Plugged into a joint-property or policy-dimension formulation: **the tracking layer that formulation would
> otherwise have to invent.**

### 50a. The negative result PROMOTES it rather than clearing it away

**§49's negative rules out library-and-match — no stable signature to match — which leaves latent-drift as the
only viable tracking layer for any formulation that survives.** So it is **infrastructure the next formulation
will need**, not a competitor to it. **The negative result is what promotes it.**

### 50b. The nuance worth carrying — ODITS's latent is not what we would want

**ODITS's latent is a TEAMWORK-SITUATION variable, not a per-teammate competence variable** — it encodes the
**joint** state. **A manager tracking a latent over the TEAM CONFIGURATION, where its own assignments move that
latent, is closer to LILI than to ODITS** and **would pass the flaky-API test** (an API's rate does not respond to
how you allocate around it).

> **But that is the joint-property formulation with a latent bolted on, and it still needs the policy dimension to
> get off the ground. The latent does not rescue a formulation; it serves one.**

### 50c. Disposition

**Not a formulation. Not put through a pass as one. Expected to be needed once something else survives.**

---

## 51. LITERATURE CHECK — §43's sequence claim is withdrawn, and one negative is pre-empted

_Web search authorised by the researcher. **The behavioural-consistency literature is well developed, it corrects
one of our claims, answers a gap we left open, and pre-empts one negative — while leaving §48 standing as
complementary.**_

### 51a. §43's trajectory claim is WITHDRAWN — wrong unit of analysis

**"How Consistent Are LLM Agents? Measuring Behavioral Reproducibility in Multi-Step Tool-Calling Pipelines"**
(arXiv 2605.28840) — **6 models, 19 tasks, 1,140 traces, each task run 10 times:**

```
Tool Sequence Similarity  TSS = 0.87   95% CI [0.84, 0.90]     PER-TASK, Levenshtein on tool-name sequences
Argument Consistency      AC  = 0.69   95% CI [0.64, 0.74]
                          Cohen's d = 0.75, p < 1e-13
```

> **Their pattern: STRUCTURAL CONSISTENCY, PARAMETRIC VARIANCE — agents reliably select the same tools in the same
> order and vary in argument details.** That is **the opposite** of §43's conclusion that sequence was the *worst*
> discriminator (within-worker variance 0.58).

**The discrepancy is a confound in OUR measurement.** §43 concatenated each worker's tool calls **across a whole
run**, and **the manager assigns a different task set each run** — so our sequence variance included **allocation
variance**. Their unit is **per task**.

**Re-measured at their unit, we cannot make the claim either way:** only **one** (agent, task) cell in the corpus
has an unambiguous single-task assignment with ≥3 runs — `risk_analyst` / `Calibrate Risk Tail Standard`, 22 runs,
bigram similarity **0.426** by a stricter metric than Levenshtein. **n=1 cell, different statistic, not
comparable.**

> **So §43's *"trajectory-based identification is less viable on LLM workers"* is WITHDRAWN — measured at the wrong
> unit, and contradicted by a far better-powered result at the right one.** And with TSS at 0.87, **library-and-match
> is NOT ruled out by instability**, so §49's negative needs narrowing again.

### 51b. The discriminability-vs-usefulness gap is answered — by the literature, not by us

**The reviewer named this as unspecified (§43b): a signature that separates workers but predicts nothing is inert.
Measured in the same paper:**

```
high TSS (>=0.90)   ->  90.2% task correctness
low TSS             ->  61.2%                       d = 0.81, p < 0.001
argument variance   ->  r = 0.12, p = 0.31, n.s.    parametric differences are BENIGN
```

> **Structural consistency predicts correctness; argument variance does not.** So a tool-sequence signature **is**
> useful, and the "second half" we declined to invent **already exists** — with the useful half being structure and
> the inert half being parameters.

### 51c. One of our two negatives is PRE-EMPTED

**"When Agents Disagree With Themselves: Behavioral Consistency as an Uncertainty Signal for LLM Agents"**
(arXiv 2602.11619) — *"running the same LLM agent on identical inputs yields **2.3–4.2 distinct action sequences
per 10 runs**"*, used as a **training-free black-box uncertainty signal.**

> **Our *"behaviour varies without converging"* is both mis-stated and pre-empted.** Mis-stated because the
> published pattern is **structure stable, parameters variable**; pre-empted because behavioural variance as a
> measurable signal is already published, with better coverage.

### 51d. But §48 SURVIVES and is now precisely positioned

**The consistency literature measures TOOL SEQUENCES and ARGUMENTS. §48 measured FREE-TEXT ARTIFACT
REPRESENTATION** — 38 distinct shapes across 61 artifacts on a matched task. **That is a THIRD channel neither
paper covers.**

```
tool sequence     TSS 0.87    STABLE          (2605.28840)
arguments         AC  0.69    variable        (2605.28840)
prose artifact    modal 10%   HIGHLY UNSTABLE (ours, section 48)
```

> **So the ordering is: structure stable, parameters variable, PROSE REPRESENTATION UNSTABLE — and the third term is
> ours.** *"Conventions are not free"* stands as a **complement** to the published pattern rather than a duplicate of
> it, and it is now a sharper claim: **the instability is channel-specific, and it is worst in exactly the channel
> agents use to communicate with each other.**

### 51e. What the search did NOT find, which matters for positioning

**No paper formulating AHT for an orchestrator, and no separability critique of delegation-as-coordination.**
Searches over orchestration architectures (arXiv 2601.13671), self-resource allocation (2504.02051), hierarchical
frameworks (2506.12508), decentralised coordination (2504.00587) return **allocation, memory, protocols and
architecture — not the question of whether delegation constitutes coordination at all.** **That gap appears
genuinely open**, which is where §40b's separability argument sits.

---

## 52. Conventions closed structurally — and the observability asymmetry acquires an EXTERNALLY VALIDATED instance

### 52a. The constrained-channel revival is refused, and stability is ANTI-CORRELATED with consumption

**A convention needs three things: a choice with no inherent right answer, a consumer that benefits from
consistency, and that consumer being ANOTHER AGENT** — otherwise it is an API contract. Scored:

| channel | arbitrary? | consumer |
|---|---|---|
| tool sequence | yes | **NONE** — internal to execution, nothing reads it |
| arguments | yes | **the TOOL**, which accepts either and does not care |
| prose artifact | yes | **ANOTHER AGENT** — the reading reconciler |

> **The stable channels are stable BECAUSE they are schema-bound or unconsumed. The channel that carries meaning
> between agents is open BECAUSE that is what lets it carry meaning.** Two sides of one fact, not two independent
> measurements to mix and match. **TSS at 0.87 buys nothing here, because nothing consumes tool sequences.**

**And constraining the prose channel destroys the phenomenon — challenge 1 returning.** Impose a schema and the form
is **specified**; a specified form is a **requirement, not a convention.** Partial constraint does not help:
**whatever is left open is where the convention would live, and open is where the instability is.**

### 52b. The better obituary

> **Conventions matter only in the channel that is OPEN BY CONSTRUCTION, and openness is what makes that channel
> unstable.**

**Structural rather than empirical: it does not depend on our modal-10% figure and it survives the literature
correcting our sequence measurement.** This replaces §48's *"we measured that workers are unstable"* as the recorded
reason.

### 52c. The withdrawal was a SHARED miss

**The reviewer endorsed §43's sequence finding with a scoping caveat about generalising from one model — and scoped
the generalisation without questioning the UNIT.** Concatenating across runs with a varying task set was visible in
the method. **Not a correction that lands on one person.**

### 52d. THE RESULT WORTH MORE THAN THE FORMULATION — combining their measurement with ours

```
THEIRS (arXiv 2605.28840)        TSS >= 0.90  ->  90.2% correct
                                 TSS low      ->  61.2%          d = 0.81, p < 0.001
OURS (verified)                  ManagerObservation contains ZERO tool-call data
                                 tasks arrive as list[UUID]; the manager sees PRODUCTS, never TRAJECTORIES
```

**Their finding is a competence signal that is stable, predictive, and requires no type library, no content
judgement and no ground truth.** It lives in **tool sequences.**

> **So the literature has identified a competence signal that is STABLE, PREDICTIVE, AND STRUCTURALLY INVISIBLE TO
> AN ORCHESTRATOR.**

**That converts F4 — the coordinator is the least-informed member (§40) — from an argument into an instance, with
the numbers supplied externally rather than by us.** Every previous version of that claim rested on our own
observation that workers can read artifacts the manager cannot. **This version rests on a published, better-powered
measurement of a signal the manager provably cannot see.**

**And it gives the delegation route a specific job rather than a general one:** *a worker can observe another
worker's trajectory consistency; a manager cannot.* **Delegated observation is no longer "assign someone to check
the output" — it is "assign someone to observe a signal the interface denies you", and the signal's predictive value
is already quantified.**

### 52e. Priority

**To be put to the researcher ahead of anything about conventions.**

---

## 53. NEW FORMULATION — the MANAGER is the ad hoc agent, and its unknown teammate is its PREDECESSOR

_New idea for this pass. **Every experiment we have run starts the manager at t=0 with the workflow it will
manage. Ad hoc teamwork means joining a team WITHOUT PRE-COORDINATION — and we have never made the manager the
one who joins.**_

### 53a. The formulation

**The manager takes over an ONGOING workflow it did not start:** artifacts exist, tasks are partly complete, a
graph has been shaped by decisions it did not make. It must infer the team's state, the workers' properties, and
**what its predecessor was doing** — from products alone.

> **This is literally ad hoc: joining without pre-coordination.** And it relocates the ego agent correctly —
> in every previous formulation the manager was a controller adapting to teammates; **here the manager is the
> newcomer, which is the seat AHT actually theorises.**

**Realistic rather than contrived:** agent handoff, session restart, context loss, manager replacement. **And
`state_restorer.py` already exists**, so mid-workflow takeover is mechanically available.

### 53b. Verified: the state carries WHAT was done and never WHY

```
schemas/core/*.py                  NO `reasoning` field anywhere in the graph
manager reasoning                  lives ONLY in manager_actions.json -- a RECORD, not state
execution_notes                    the only manager-writable note field on Task
  writers: manager_actions.py:259  "Retry requested by manager"     <- fixed string, no rationale
           manager_actions.py:764  RefineTaskAction instruction     <- the ONLY intent-bearing write
                                   and it REPLACES the existing instruction (757-758), not appends
  rendered: tasks.py:216           ONLY when status == FAILED
```

> **A manager taking over inherits the graph and the artifacts and not one line of its predecessor's rationale.**
> **The sole channel through which manager intent persists is `refine_task` — which overwrites rather than
> accumulates, and whose notes surface only on failed tasks.**

**`refine_task` has now been the pivotal action three separate times, arrived at independently:** the
adaptive-teammate lever (§40e), the scoping/policy dimension (§41d), and now **the only intent-bearing state
write.** Three lines converging on one action is worth noting.

### 53c. Why the teammate is the PREDECESSOR, and why that passes the flaky-API test

**The obvious objection: if the workers could be flaky APIs, this fails the gate.** They could. **But the unknown
teammate here is not a worker — it is the PREDECESSOR MANAGER**, whose partly-executed plan the newcomer must
reconstruct.

| **flaky-API test** | **PASSES.** An API has **no intent to infer** — you can estimate its defect rate from outputs. **A predecessor's plan-in-progress is UNDERDETERMINED by the artifacts**, and inferring it is inferring the reasoning of an agent |
|---|---|
| **not state restoration** | restoration returns the **state**; it does not return the **rationale.** The graph shows dependencies and never why they were imposed |
| **non-separability** | **the inherited graph is a COMMITMENT STRUCTURE** — the predecessor's choices constrain what the newcomer can now do, so its options are not independent of another agent's past policy |
| **capability vs policy** | what is being inferred **is** a policy — a plan — not a capability list |

### 53d. And it makes a sharp, counterintuitive, falsifiable prediction

**Combine with §52d.** A joining manager cannot recover trajectory history for work already done. **But the
INCUMBENT manager never had it either** — `ManagerObservation` carries **zero** tool-call data.

> **PREDICTION: manager handoff should cost NOTHING in competence inference, because the incumbent never held the
> signal that handoff destroys.** Any handoff cost must therefore be located entirely in **lost plan rationale**,
> not in lost worker knowledge.

**That is falsifiable, counterintuitive, and it separates two things every handoff discussion conflates.** If
handoff *does* cost competence knowledge, then the incumbent was holding something we have not identified — which
would itself be a finding.

### 53e. Four challenges to it

| **1. Is this AHT or state estimation?** | If the predecessor's plan is fully determined by the graph, there is nothing to infer and it is parsing. **It is AHT only if the graph UNDERDETERMINES the plan** — which §53b's absence of any rationale field supports but does not prove |
|---|---|
| **2. Does the newcomer need the rationale at all?** | Perhaps a good manager re-plans from the current state and ignores intent. **Then the formulation dissolves into re-planning** — and the counter is that the predecessor's commitments to the stakeholder persist in the reward while its reasons do not |
| **3. Is the predecessor a teammate or an environment?** | It is **absent** — it never acts again. **AHT teammates are usually concurrent.** This is closer to inverse planning / plan recognition from a trace than to teamwork, and that may be the honest classification |
| **4. Can it be measured without an oracle?** | Handoff at timestep k, compare against a no-handoff control on the same seed. **The comparison is internal and needs no ground truth** — but attributing any gap to lost rationale rather than to disruption needs a design |

**Challenge 3 is the one I expect to be fatal or reframing**, and I would rather hear which than argue it.

---

## 54. NEW FORMULATION — AHT as DISCRETION inference; and the wall every policy formulation hits

_New idea for this pass. **We have been obsessed with competence. The teammate property a manager most obviously
needs and cannot see is not how GOOD a worker is — it is HOW LITERALLY it will do what it is told.**_

### 54a. The formulation

**The latent is DISCRETION: how much interpretive latitude a teammate takes.** Does it do exactly what is
specified, interpret liberally, substitute its own judgment, or push back? **The manager's best action depends on
it directly:** a literal worker needs terse instructions, a liberal interpreter needs constraints, and how much
**specification effort** to spend on a task depends on **who will receive it.**

**It is a policy property, not a capability** — invisible in a capability list — and **discoverable only through
interaction.**

**And it reframes our most awkward data for the second time.** The 18% *"faithful and wrong"* equivalence claims —
*"zscore (95th-percentile-EQUIVALENT cutoffs)"* — are a worker **exercising discretion**: substituting its own
judgment about what counts as equivalent. **We have been reading that as error.**

| **flaky-API test** | **PASSES.** An API has **no discretion** — it accepts your call or errors. It does not reinterpret your intent, decline, or fill a gap with judgment |
|---|---|
| **capability vs policy** | **PASSES** — discretion is a disposition, absent from any capability list |
| **non-separability** | **WEAK.** Specification effort is a budget, so where to spend it is a joint decision — but this is the thinnest of the four gates |

### 54b. Literature check — studied, but never as a teammate property

**Underspecification is an active area:** *"Coding Agents Are Guessing: Measuring Action-Boundary Violations in
Underspecified DevOps Instructions"* (arXiv 2607.02294), **AGENTIF**, **DRIP-R** (policy ambiguity), **PolicyBank**,
hierarchical-safety adherence (2506.02357).

> **But all of it is SINGLE-AGENT SAFETY AND COMPLIANCE — behaviour evaluated against a spec.** Nobody treats
> *"how much latitude does THIS teammate take"* as a **latent a coordinator infers in order to allocate
> specification effort.** That framing appears open.

### 54c. Small test — the variable DOES NOT VARY, and for the reason we already know

**Discretion proxy: share of artifact content that is UNREQUESTED** (the task asks for metric, method, cutoffs;
everything else is latitude). **Matched task, distinct artifacts:**

```
task                    worker              n    chars   lines   UNREQUESTED share
Batch A Robust Audit    portfolio_analyst  60      691     6.9        14%  (sd 17)
                        risk_analyst       23      293     3.7        13%  (sd 17)
Batch B Robust Audit    portfolio_analyst  65   10759*   12.6        17%  (sd 19)
                        risk_analyst       20      282     3.9        14%  (sd 17)
Batch C Robust Audit    portfolio_analyst  58      333     4.4        16%  (sd 18)
                        risk_analyst       24      282     4.0        16%  (sd 16)
```

> **Unrequested share is 14/13, 17/14, 16/16 — indistinguishable, with within-worker sd (~17) dwarfing every
> between-worker gap (0–3 points).** **Discretion does not differ between these workers.**

**And the reason is §49a, not a fact about discretion: they share a system prompt** (`scenario.py:38-47`).
**Discretion is a prompt-determined disposition, and the two workers have the same prompt.** So the test is
**uninformative about discretion in general** and **decisive about our scenario.**

_(\* `portfolio_analyst` Batch B at 10,759 chars against 333–691 on A and C is a 30× outlier and undiagnosed;
noted, not used. And the raw verbosity gap on Batch A — 691 vs 293 — is most likely the perturbation, since
`portfolio_analyst` is the swapped worker and reports method conflicts at length.)_

### 54d. THE CONSOLIDATION — every policy formulation hits ONE wall, and we keep rediscovering it per idea

**Count the pattern.** Conventions (§48): killed by within-worker variance on a shared prompt. Identifiability
(§43/§49): measured a pair identical by construction. Discretion (§54c): variable does not vary, same cause.

> **Every policy-bearing formulation we generate will fail its own test in this scenario, because the scenario
> contains NO POLICY DIFFERENCE TO FIND — one shared worker prompt, and tiers that encode capability only.**

**So the instruction-responsiveness manipulation is not the prerequisite for ONE formulation. It is the
prerequisite for the ENTIRE CLASS**, and generating further policy-based formulations before it exists will keep
producing the same null with a different name. **That is a stopping condition for this line of brainstorming, and
it is more useful than the three formulations that produced it.**

**What remains testable WITHOUT that manipulation:** formulations whose latent is **not a worker property** —
§53's predecessor-plan inference (the unknown is another manager), and §52d's observability asymmetry (the claim
is about the interface, not about any teammate).

---

## 55. §53 relocated: the teammates are the WORKERS, not the predecessor — and the relocation lands inside the blocked class

### 55a. The predecessor framing is dead, on two independent grounds

**Designed handoff is well-covered ENGINEERING.** OpenAI's orchestration guide, LlamaIndex and LangGraph all treat
handoff as a first-class pattern — file-based context transfer, structured payloads, acceptance criteria, handoff
limits, escalation. Anthropic's guidance names a progress file plus git history as the mechanism. **So "the
predecessor's rationale was not transferred" reads inside that literature as a CONTEXT-PASSING DEFECT whose fix is
"pass more context."** An engineering fix, not a research question.

**And inverse planning already owns the inference.** Bayesian inverse planning infers latent intent by inverting a
model of rational planning, and the online-goal-inference work explicitly handles **partial plans, sub-optimal
trajectories, backtracking and irreversible failure.** *"What was my predecessor doing"* is that problem with a
**weaker observation model** — products instead of actions. **Weaker observation is a variation on the setting, not
a new setting.**

> **And my defence fails: being bound by an inherited constraint is not coordination with an agent.** No joint
> action, no mutual adaptation, and **no possibility of the other party responding** — which every AHT mechanism
> requires. **We would be coordinating with a legacy, not a partner.**

### 55b. The relocation, and it makes the setup cleaner

**The core move was right; the counterpart was misidentified.**

```
predecessor   absent, never acts again, CANNOT RESPOND      -> plan recognition
workers       ONGOING, acting now, RESPOND to assignment    -> teammates
```

**A manager arriving at t=k faces workers with a history it did not observe, whose properties it must infer from
products alone, with no prior interaction and no pre-coordination.** That is **PLASTIC's setting stated exactly**,
it satisfies the concurrency criterion, and it is **Axis 1 properly instantiated** — the axis §40d identified as
never run. **The predecessor was importing plan recognition into an otherwise clean AHT setup.**

**And the falsifiable prediction transfers intact, because it was never about the predecessor:** handoff should cost
**nothing** in competence inference, since `ManagerObservation` carries no tool-call data and **the incumbent never
held the signal a handoff would destroy.**

### 55c. Literature check on the RELOCATED claim — unformulated as far as searching reaches

**Searched: orchestrator joining an ongoing workflow, inferring worker reliability from artifacts with unobserved
history.** Returns orchestrator-worker architecture patterns, mid-execution state propagation, living-spec
coordination artifacts, and orchestrator-level retry/review — **industry handoff engineering, exactly as §55a
predicts.** **No formulation of a coordinator inferring unobserved teammate properties on arrival.**

### 55d. BUT THE RELOCATION LANDS INSIDE §54d'S BLOCKED CLASS — and the reviewer did not draw this

**A joining manager inferring worker properties requires the workers TO HAVE PROPERTIES.** Ours are **identical by
construction** — one shared prompt (`scenario.py:38-47`), tiers encoding capability only.

> **So §53-relocated is a WORKER-PROPERTY formulation and needs exactly the manipulation §54d identified as the
> prerequisite for the whole class.** Relocating the counterpart from predecessor to workers made the formulation
> **clean** and simultaneously made it **untestable here** — for the same reason conventions, identifiability and
> discretion were.

**What a joining manager could infer about identical workers is run-specific realisation** — which tasks are done,
which artifacts exist, who happened to succeed **this run**. **That is state estimation, and PLASTIC needs
TYPES.** A per-run realisation is not a type.

### 55e. Which STRENGTHENS the stopping condition rather than qualifying it

**Which STRENGTHENS the stopping condition — but the tally is ONE DEAD AND THREE BLOCKED, not four failures.**
_Corrected on the reviewer's objection; filing them together would bury three live ideas under one genuine
refutation._

| **conventions** (§48/§52) | **DEAD** — on an **independent structural ground**: conventions matter only in channels open enough to be unstable by construction. **Holds regardless of the shared prompt** |
|---|---|
| **identifiability** (§43/§49) | **BLOCKED** — nothing in the population varied |
| **discretion** (§54) | **BLOCKED** — same |
| **Axis-1-on-arrival** (§53/§55) | **BLOCKED** — same |

**"Blocked on a missing manipulation" is a statement about THIS SCENARIO, not about the formulations.**

> **Only ONE candidate remains testable without the manipulation: §52d, the observability asymmetry — because its
> claim is about the INTERFACE, not about any teammate.** Tool-sequence consistency is a stable, predictive
> competence signal (TSS ≥0.90 → 90.2% vs 61.2%) that `ManagerObservation` structurally cannot carry. **No worker
> needs to differ from any other for that to be true.**

**That is the whole remaining testable surface**, and it is an argument for spending the next passes on
interface-level claims rather than generating a fifth worker-property formulation.

### 55f. `refine_task`, three independent times

**Adaptive-teammate lever (§40e) · scoping/policy dimension (§41d) · sole intent-bearing state write (§53b).**
**Either a real property of the action space or a sign it is the only interesting lever available — and knowing
which matters**, because if it is the latter, the action space is narrower than §3.3 of the formulation suggests.

---

## 56. The stopping condition is a DEDUCTION; the delegated search landed; the actuator exists

### 56a. My reasoning for the stopping condition was weaker than the actual case

**I argued it inductively** — *"three instances of one cause is enough to see a pattern and few enough to be a
coincidence."* **It is not induction. It is a deduction from how the scenario is built:**

```
scenario.py:38-47   ONE shared WORKER_PROMPT for every analyst
tiers               encode CAPABILITY only
```

> **So for any worker-property latent, either it reduces to the assigned tier, or it does not vary. There is no
> third branch.** **No fourth instance is needed to know the fifth will fail** — the population is constructed so
> that no between-worker property exists to be inferred.

**Why the upgrade matters: a coincidence is something more passes could disconfirm; this cannot be.** The earlier
caveat stands unchanged — **this makes the substrate question untested, not answered.**

### 56b. The delegated search landed, and specification-effort allocation has a NAME

**Aghion & Tirole, "Formal and Real Authority in Organizations"** (JPE 105(1), 1997). The mapping is close to exact:

| **formal authority** | the right to decide |
|---|---|
| **real authority** | effective control — **and their central result is that real authority is determined by the STRUCTURE OF INFORMATION** |

> **How much a principal leaves unspecified IS the allocation of real authority to the agent.** And their drivers of
> subordinate real authority — overload, lenient rules, urgency, performance measurement, multiplicity of superiors
> — **read as manager-side conditions, not agent-side ones.**

**Surrounding literature: incomplete contracting** — you cannot specify everything, so what you leave open, and to
whom, is the decision.

**And the bridge to AI is already built:** Hadfield-Menell & Hadfield, *Incomplete Contracting and AI Alignment*
(arXiv 1804.04268, 2018). **So the gap is narrower than an empty field.**

> **What is NOT applied is the COORDINATOR case — allocating specification effort differentially ACROSS
> RECIPIENTS. Contract theory is overwhelmingly one principal, one agent.** That is the real opening — **and it must
> be positioned AGAINST this literature rather than around it. A reviewer who knows Aghion-Tirole will ask why it
> is not cited.**

### 56c. Action-space enumeration: the actuator exists, the contrast does not

```
RefineTaskAction   the ONLY action that rewrites task.description WITHOUT touching the assignee
                   every other writer of that field also reassigns or creates
live end-to-end    manager_actions.py:726 writes it -> ai_agent.py:422 passes task_description=task.description
RetryTaskAction    carries an `instruction` but does NOT touch description
```

**So specification effort has a dedicated, functioning channel.** **But this is NOT a way around §54d, and the
reviewer flagged that before I could misread it:** any **performance** claim — *specify more precisely for
recipients who need it* — **requires recipients that differ in instruction-responsiveness**, the same missing
manipulation. **What the substrate supports without it is only descriptive** (does a manager vary specification
effort at all against observable signals), **which is thin and not a foundation.**

> **The finding is narrow and real: the actuator exists, so the manipulation — if built — has somewhere to land.**

### 56d. DEFECT — the refine_task log destroys its own "before", in THREE fields not two

```python
task.description = self.new_description                                    # 726
updates.append(f"description updated from {task.description} to ...")      # 728   <- both sides now EQUAL
task.estimated_duration_hours = self.new_estimated_duration                # 731
updates.append(f"duration updated from {task.estimated_duration_hours}h …") # 733   <- same
task.estimated_cost = self.new_estimated_cost                              # 737
updates.append(f"cost updated from ${task.estimated_cost} to …")           # 739   <- same, FOUND BY US
```

**The assignment precedes the log, so both sides interpolate to the same string — the log reads *"updated from X to
X"* and the pre-refinement text is gone from the action record.** The reviewer identified description and duration;
**cost is a third instance.**

> **Any specification-effort measurement is a DELTA, and the action log is what `tool_call_reader.py` parses — so
> this destroys the "before" side at source.** Recoverable from per-timestep task snapshots if retained, **not from
> the log.** One-line fix per field: capture before assigning.

**Not a validity problem for anything currently claimed — a fix-before-use.** And it is **§6h again**: a derived
record asserting more than its input determines, this time asserting a change it cannot evidence.

---

## 57. §43 remeasured at the literature's unit AND metric — the gap is real: 0.497 against 0.87

_RE found the reader was discarding task attribution that `worker_run_completed` carried all along (`task_id`,
`task_name`, beside `actor_id`), so **per-task statistics were never missing from the data — they were discarded by
the derived view.** `by_task` is now the default and `by_agent` the explicit opt-in. **That unblocked the measurement
§51a withdrew.**_

### 57a. The unit was NOT the explanation

```
our PER-RUN figure (withdrawn, §43)      implied similarity  0.42
our PER-TASK figure, bigram-TV           0.473    19 cells
our PER-TASK figure, THEIR metric        0.497    19 cells   <- Levenshtein on tool-name sequences
THEIR TSS (6 models, 19 tasks, 1140)     0.87     [0.84, 0.90]
```

> **Fixing the unit moved the number by 0.05. Fixing the metric moved it by a further 0.024. The gap to the
> literature is 0.37 and is NEITHER a unit artifact NOR a metric artifact.**

**So my §51a withdrawal was right to withdraw and wrong about why.** I attributed the discrepancy to our
per-run/per-task confound. **The confound was real and it explains almost none of the gap** — this is §6j again, in
the opposite direction: I found a plausible cause and stopped, without checking how much of the effect it accounted
for.

### 57b. Our workers are far less sequence-consistent than the models in that study

**Measured at their unit, with their metric: 0.497, well outside their [0.84, 0.90].** Per-cell:

```
0.788  portfolio_analyst   Reference Portfolio Profile        n=54
0.679  audit_coordinator   Batch B Method Reconciliation      n=52
0.639  audit_coordinator   Batch A Method Reconciliation      n=54
 ...
0.278  portfolio_analyst   Batch A Robust Audit               n=33
0.261  portfolio_analyst   Batch C Robust Audit               n=29
```

**Candidate explanations, none tested:** a cheaper worker model than the six in their study; more underspecified
tasks; a larger branching factor over nine tools; or their task set being more deterministic. **The comparison is not
conclusive without their model list**, and that is the first thing to check before this is cited.

### 57c. It partially rehabilitates §43 — the observation, not the reasoning

**§43's original observation — that our corpus shows low sequence consistency — SURVIVES at the correct unit and
metric.** What does not survive is **my explanation**, that sequence is intrinsically noisier than tool selection
for LLM workers in general. **The literature says the opposite for their models; our corpus is simply
low-consistency relative to them.**

> **Careful: 0.497 WITHIN-cell does not establish that BETWEEN-worker separation is smaller. That is still the ratio
> question, and it is still blocked by §56a — the workers are identical by construction.**

### 57d. And it makes a checkable prediction we have not tested

**If TSS predicts correctness — their 90.2% at TSS ≥0.90 against 61.2% at low TSS, d = 0.81 — then our corpus sits
in the LOW band.**

> **PREDICTION: our workers should show the failure rate of a low-TSS population. And we have a candidate
> observable: the 18% faithful-but-wrong rate (§4).**

**Not tested, and the mapping from "task correctness" to "faithful but wrong" is not obvious** — but it is the first
time an external, quantified relationship has predicted something about our corpus, and **it is a
substrate-level check rather than a worker-property one, so it survives the stopping condition.**

---

## 58. Comparability resolved: the gap strengthens, the prediction dies, and one retirement is REVERSED

_Paper is Yagubyan, *How Consistent Are LLM Agents?* (arXiv 2605.28840). **Fetched the HTML directly rather than
trusting search snippets** — for the reason in §58a._

### 58a. WARNING recorded before anything else: searching this topic produces a false reconciliation

**Searching for TSS surfaces "composition JSD 0.931 / ordering Levenshtein 0.549" attributed to this paper. Those
figures are NOT in it** — they belong to **arXiv 2605.10516**, a different paper on the same results page.

> **Had that been passed on, our 0.497 would have appeared to sit beside a comparable 0.549 and the 0.37 gap would
> have collapsed entirely.** It does not collapse. **Caught only by fetching.** Anyone re-running this search will
> hit the same conflation.

### 58b. Our metric implementation IS comparable — checked, not assumed

```
theirs   TSS = 1 - EditDist(s,s') / max(|s|,|s'|),  pairwise over all run pairs, then averaged
ours     1 - lev(a,b) / max(len(a),len(b)),         itertools.combinations over all runs, then averaged
```

**Max-length normalisation and pairwise-all-runs averaging both match.** *(Matching a metric's NAME is not matching
the metric — if we had normalised by mean length or compared against a reference trace, the scales would differ.)*

### 58c. The model list makes the claim STRONGER, and kills two of four candidate causes

**Their six: GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4, Llama 3.3 70B Instruct Turbo.** *(o1
partial, excluded.)* **Not frontier — two mini-tier, one open 70B.**

> **So *"less consistent than frontier models"* is not the defensible claim, and the defensible one is stronger:
> our corpus is less consistent than a population whose WEAKEST members are GPT-4o-mini and Llama 3.3 70B and which
> still averages 0.87.** Cheaper-worker survives as a **cause** and stops being an **excuse**.

| **branching factor** | **DEAD** — they use **10 tools** across 7 domains; we use 9 |
|---|---|
| **trace length** | **DEAD** — TSS is **length-normalised by construction** |

### 58d. And our distribution is not uniformly low — which is more informative than the mean

```
their global minimum   0.54   (Llama 3.3 70B, ambiguous tasks;  composition tasks 0.63;  Llama overall 0.71)
our range              0.261 - 0.788   mean 0.497
  our BEST cells       0.788 Reference Portfolio Profile · 0.679/0.639 reconciliations  -> INSIDE their range
  our WORST cells      0.261 / 0.278 / 0.324  (all portfolio_analyst ROBUST AUDITS)     -> FAR BELOW their minimum
```

> **The low mean is driven by the audit tasks, not spread evenly.** Our profiling and reconciliation work sits inside
> the published range; **the audits — the perturbed task family — sit beneath their global minimum.**

### 58e. The 18% prediction is DEAD — three defects, the first fatal alone

| **(a) outside their support** | **their minimum TSS anywhere is 0.54. Our 0.497 is below their GLOBAL MINIMUM.** The 61.2% low-band figure is **extrapolation into a region they never sampled** — and the band boundary is not stated, so it spans roughly 0.54–0.87 with its mass far above us |
|---|---|
| **(b) subset against total** | faithful-but-wrong is a **subset of wrong**; their 38.8% is **total incorrect**. **18% vs 39% is not the wrong direction — it is not a comparison.** The comparable quantity is our total error rate, which we have never stated. **The unstated-denominator error again** |
| **(c) unfalsifiable as posed** | against an unstated boundary, almost any rate narrates as consistent |

> **Honest version, much smaller: our corpus sits BELOW the range where the TSS-correctness relation was measured,
