**The trap avoided (receipts):** misaddressing does NOT break delivery. `send_direct_message`
validates nothing (service.py:89-108) and the manager's `recent_messages` is
`get_all_messages()[:message_window]` — ALL traffic, not manager-addressed traffic
(interface.py:161-164; rendered as `sender → receiver | type: content`,
structured_manager.py:274-281). `to_agent` is decorative from the manager's seat. Consequences:
**no engine fix is needed for the ask cell's return path**; but workers are not intentionally
addressing the manager — they broadcast into a room the manager happens to overhear, so **a reply to
an ask must be identified by content and timing, never by addressee**.

**Speech act — RE confirmed:** 82.1% declarative (completion reports), 14.3% interrogative. One
interrogative is a design gift: `portfolio_analyst` spontaneously broadcast a request for the
95th-percentile reference cutoffs — **a worker deprived of a capability asking for exactly what the
perturbation took away, unmanufactured**. S3's manufactured behaviour has a natural precedent.

**Consumption — LS/RE confirmed, RR refuted: 0 of 864 manager actions cite a worker message** (37
message-carrying runs). *[P14 tag, added 2026-08-05 where the number lives: SETUP-LEVEL — a fact
about what this build's workers spontaneously emitted against this renderer; a prior, not a portable
result. See §100 for the licensing limits and §103 for the tag.]* The raw scan's 28 candidates hand-classified: 26 stakeholder/own-traffic; the
2 worker-looking hits both REFUTED on inspection — each was the manager consuming the ANNOUNCEMENT
channel, misattributed to the worker channel by the scan regex (both `full`-condition runs; one cites
capability content absent from any worker message, one precedes every worker message in its run).
P13 applied by its own author before the result shipped. Causal half reported and labelled: +15.8pp
assign-rate after worker messages, not quotable at this n, exactly as pre-flagged.

**Interpretive note (lead, marked as interpretation):** the corpus now shows a channel-consumption
HIERARCHY from two free checks — the announcement channel is consumed (allocation +0.611; cited in
manager reasoning, even showing up as CHECK-4's false positives) while the worker-message channel is
never cited (0/864). Study 1's premise — channels genuinely differ in consumption — has corpus
support on both ends before a single run is spent. RR's 20–50% was the only prediction that would
have validated the worker→manager half from the corpus; its refutation means that half rests on the
ask cell's manufactured salience, and a flash-only null there is pre-labelled model-specific (§93).
*[Corrected by §100: the "hierarchy by channel" reading is refuted — stakeholder messages on the SAME
channel are cited 34/864. The discriminating features are addressee and actionability, not channel;
and CHECK-4's 0/864 licenses a claim about spontaneous, misaddressed, declarative traffic only. The
ask cell's design prior is the stakeholder 34/864, not the worker 0/864.]*

**Design consequences adopted:** (1) `message_window` defaults to 10 of ALL traffic — late-episode
stakeholder chatter can crowd an ask's reply out of the manager's rendered window; window size and
ask timing are DESIGN PARAMETERS, set deliberately in the cell spec. (2) **Third logging record**
added to the study-wide spec: message id, sender, timestep, and whether it entered the manager's
rendered window — the last being the only fact that establishes the manager COULD have consumed it.
(3) RE authorized to draft the §97 cell-ordering spec as free work.

## 100. CHECK-4 reproduction — 0/864 verified twice; the lead's mechanism refuted; addressee mechanism adopted (2026-08-04)

**Reproduction:** identical output except one row-order flap — `check_worker_messages.py:280` sorts a
printed table on count alone, so equal totals tie-break on set iteration order (confirmed flapping
across randomized-hash runs; same defect class as the 8732ed1 fix, in a script written AFTER it).
**Convention adopted, replacing per-script patches: every printed ordering carries a total sort key**
(`(-count, str(key))`). Two instances in two scripts; the third was likelier than not.

**The two consumption candidates verified by a STRUCTURAL discriminator** (no string re-reading): in
`silent`/`control` runs no announcement exists, so a message-reference there cannot be announcement
misattribution — 28/40 hits are announcement-impossible, and all 28 are stakeholder-directed; the
`full`-run candidate matches `specific_announcement` verbatim. **0/864 stands, verified two
independent ways.** Bonus instrument warning for the study: the announcement text OVERLAPS the static
agent-card text (two silent-run hits read "the screening_analyst, who specializes in mean-plus-two-SD
screening" — the card, not an announcement). **Any announcement-consumption detector must be
condition-gated or keyed to announcement-unique phrasing; a string detector over-counts.**

**The lead's window/authority hypothesis is REFUTED, with the receipt that replaces it:** stakeholder
and worker messages travel the identical path, window, and renderer — and manager reasoning cites
stakeholder messages **34/864** vs worker messages **0/864**. Same pipe, 34 vs 0: the pipe is not the
variable. Newest-first slicing (service.py:326-328) puts fresh messages at the TOP of the window —
the burial mechanism the hypothesis needed is not what the code does. **Adopted working
interpretation (marked as interpretation): the discriminating features are ADDRESSED-TO-ME and
ACTIONABLE-BY-ME.** The renderer displays the addressee (`sender → receiver`,
structured_manager.py:274-280), so a misaddressed message arrives visibly not-for-me; 48/56 worker
sends are addressed to nonexistent ids and 82% are status declaratives about work the manager already
sees in artifacts. **The honest headline: workers talk into the void, and the manager correctly
ignores mail addressed to someone else.** The manager is behaving reasonably, not failing.

**Narrower licensed claim (adopted; §99 annotated):** CHECK-4 tested spontaneous, misaddressed,
declarative traffic. A message addressed TO the manager, answering a question the manager ASKED,
bearing on a decision the manager OWNS, is untested — and its design prior is the stakeholder 34/864,
not the worker 0/864. The ask cell is not designed against a zero.

**Design consequences:** (1) the ask reply must be manager-addressed — worker-prompt instruction plus
a logged addressee check (joins the study-wide logging spec as its fourth record); (2) window SIZE
demoted as a parameter (newest-first protects a t+1 reply); ask TIMING retained; (3) the §99
spontaneous interrogative broadcast is the strongest single S3 datum and sits in the consumable
addressee class — broadcast renders as `→ ALL`, not visibly someone else's mail.

**Reviewer's self-scoring, recorded:** their CHECK-1-derived correction ("direct assertion in prompt")
moved in the right direction and stopped at the first difference found — the operative features were
addressee and directive force, not directness. Refuted at 20–50% vs 0/864.

## 102. P14 — researcher's principle adopted; the kill re-audit; what changes and what stands (2026-08-05)

**Researcher directive (2026-08-05, verbatim in substance):** ideas should be inferred from past
experiments only MARGINALLY. Setups are changeable — a good idea must never be discarded because the
current scenario or corpus cannot host or support it. Past experiments are most likely obsolete (ours
were generated under the abandoned deficiency perturbation, old prompts, old scenario).

**The defect this exposes in the §90 convergence, stated plainly:** ranking by information-per-cost
measured "information" largely against the OLD corpus — which was generated by the abandoned design,
and therefore systematically favors ideas the old setup happened to express and kills ideas it
happened not to host. Selection bias in the selection procedure. Several P-constraints flagged pieces
of this (RE's "affords, not managers generically"; the P2 caveats on every corpus check) but the
ranking did not fully honor them.

**P14 (ADOPTED):**
> Every kill or retirement must state its LEVEL. **Idea-level** = an inferential defect that survives
> any setup change. **Setup-level** = a fact about the current build; such kills SHELVE the idea (with
> the reviving setup change and its cost named), they do not bury it. Scenario redesign is a
> legitimate cost line, not a disqualifier. Symmetrically: setup-level SUPPORT is a prior to
> re-establish, never a result to lean on — old corpora go obsolete.

**The re-audit of every §88–§91 kill, by level:**

| candidate | recorded verdict | level on audit | new status |
|---|---|---|---|
| S6 commensurability | "premise false in-scenario" | **SETUP-level, entirely** — the reconcile consumer is representation-insensitive BY CONSTRUCTION; CHECK-3's null is a fact about that consumer, not about the idea | **SHELVED, not dead — leading study-2 candidate.** Revival: one representation-sensitive consumer task (scenario redesign, now a legitimate cost). Study 1's builds (perturbation, trace substrate) are prerequisites S6 wants anyway |
| S7 change-vs-rate | "retires on cost" | **Mixed.** The variance pricing is OLD-CORPUS (setup-level; a new scenario/DV design may have different variance structure). The matching-definability question is per-perturbation, answerable on paper | **SHELVED pending new-setup variance.** Re-price after the gate pair exists; the definability question travels with whatever perturbation is chosen |
| S8 marginal value | "no neutral baseline" | **IDEA-level primarily** (the baseline is a free parameter in ANY setup; bracketing is the partial fix) + one setup-level half (tool-dominated outcomes) | Stays retired on the idea-level defect; the bracketing design noted as the only revival form |
| S2 IV-existence | "unpredictability may not be settable" (§48 variance) | **SETUP-level** — §48's within-worker variance was measured under old prompts | Objection DEMOTED from binding to re-measure-under-new-setup |
| S1/S2 floor | already narrowed §86–87 | resolved by design | unchanged |
| S5 "re-run not novelty" | prior coverage | idea-level bookkeeping (true regardless of setup) | unchanged |
| §91 factorial unaffordability | interaction needs crossed cells | **Mixed**: cell-count arithmetic is setup-free; the 69/arm pricing is old-corpus | Main-effects scope stands on arithmetic + the researcher's run constraint; re-price interactions if the new setup's variance differs materially |

**Symmetric application to the chosen direction's own support:** +0.611, 34/864-vs-0/864, and the
worker-comms behaviour are all OLD-SETUP evidence — held as PRIORS the design re-establishes (the
cell structure already does this for CHECK-1), never as results study 1 cites. The direction's case
is restated on idea-level grounds: the channel-dissociation gap is a fact about the LITERATURE, not
our corpus (G1/G8 — pending full-length reads); the ask channel's novelty is setup-independent; LLM
teammates having tellable types is a property of the object of study, not of worker_replacement.

**What does NOT change:** the converged direction stands — but on its idea-level justification, with
corpus evidence demoted to marginal support. The gate sequence, the two perturbation requirements,
and the 2-SSR ask are unchanged. S6's reinstatement as shelved makes it the default study-2
candidate rather than a competitor to study 1, since study 1's infrastructure feeds it.

researcher in full.

## 104. P14 follow-through — a latent silent-omission defect fixed; a study-2 foreclosure constraint on trace rendering (2026-08-05)

RE, committed at 50b7781:

**The re-price path was already broken, quietly — found because P14 made it worth checking.** Under
any new setup, `check_announcement.collect()`'s old-setup constants (`_robust` key suffix,
`flag_outliers_zscore` literal) would match zero rows, and `check_variance` would price the nine
secondary DVs, SILENTLY OMIT THE PRIMARY ONE, and print a normal-looking table. Same failure class
as the two-layout denominator: **a plausible-looking number is the failure mode nobody re-checks.**
Fixed three ways (constants hoisted and named; every skip counted and printed by reason — the 78→74
attrition is now visible; a `!! PRIMARY DV ABSENT` banner), and verified by SIMULATING a mismatched
setup rather than by reasoning: 75 skips printed, 0/78 carrying the primary DV, unmissable.
Byte-stability re-verified.

**S6 non-foreclosure, elevated into the trace-rendering decision's inputs (spec §7):** two build
constraints that cost nothing now and are expensive to retrofit — the perturbation must not assume
the consumer is numeric-extraction-only; and **the trace substrate must not render operands in a
normalised form** — a renderer that tidies operands into uniform shape destroys exactly the surface
variation a representation-sensitive consumer would key on, and recovery means re-rendering every
episode. The trace-rendering decision now has two INDEPENDENT axes: how much to render (cost), and
whether to normalise (study-2 foreclosure).

**RE's P14 self-assessment recorded:** several §83 costings priced clusters within-the-existing-setup
— the wrong frame for at least S6 and S2; the setup-change option existed and was not offered.
**S6's setup-change costing authorized (free, estimation only)** — it makes the shelf discussion
concrete for the researcher.

## 105. S6 setup-change costing delivered — ~1.5–2d, with the validity crux named (2026-08-05)

RE, `S6_SETUP_CHANGE_COSTING.md`, commit bbd8969. Estimation only. Key content:

**~1.5–2d — cheaper than the perturbation build**, because ground truth, artifact reader, and scoring
harness exist; new work is one task definition + one producer-contract change.

**The validity crux: the consumer must be an AGENT reading artifact text, not a tool parsing it.**
The obvious build (another `analyze_audit_artifacts` operation) is invalid — the experimenter's
regex would BE the representation-sensitive consumer (CHECK-3's P3 objection inverted: there the
parser was a cleared nuisance at 0.000; here it would be the entire effect). Structural receipt: every
current operation compresses the artifact to one scalar via `artifact_metric` BEFORE any consumer
sees it — form is discarded upstream by construction, which is the mechanism behind CHECK-3's null.
`read_audit_artifact` (scenario.py:461-473) already returns raw content to a worker — buildable with
no plumbing.

**Proposed task — per-column discrepancy attribution:** read both producers' artifacts, report which
column carries the largest robust-vs-screen discrepancy. Needs multiple fields (layout determines
recoverability); needs a join on column identity across producers (non-comparable-operands in
literal form — `dti` vs `debt-to-income` IS the task); truth exists per column
(`_flag_count`, scenario.py:209-215); the answer is a single token, so DV extraction is categorical
and cannot reintroduce the parser. Producer contract carries per-column detail and must NOT template
it — natural variation is the IV (the non-normalisation axis, arriving from the other direction).
Removes no tool from anyone (core-tool rule respected; the task simply has no single-call shortcut).

**Coexistence: NO — own scenario variant/arm** (firm recommendation, accepted): adding a task changes
workload/timesteps/action counts, breaking comparability with the corpus baseline that the +0.611
estimate and all variance figures come from. Study 2 cannot borrow study 1's variance estimates —
which P14 already said.

**Smoke tests, both EPISODE-FREE, order load-bearing:** (1) synthetic-format ablation first — one
set of per-column numbers rendered in k formats with information content identical by construction;
any accuracy difference is attributable to form alone. ~1h to write, k×n consumer model calls (small
flash spend, NOT zero — researcher-visible). This decides whether the idea is real. (2) corpus smoke
second — existing artifact pairs fed to the consumer offline (~a few hundred flash calls); the weaker
question of whether the effect survives naturally-occurring formats. **P3 fake-mechanisms with
separators, named in advance:** our own parser (avoided by construction); format-correlates-with-
trace (real — 18/20 JSON operands were zscore-produced; separator: upstream-only trace
stratification, decided before reading); length (separator: control or band).

**Honest scope:** this prices the CONDITION S6 needs, not S6's value — a representation-sensitive
consumer makes the question askable, not the answer interesting.

Status: smoke tests NOT authorized — they cost model calls and S6's promotion is exactly what the
researcher is deciding on the shelf; offered to the researcher as a decision input.

## 106. REALISM RULING (researcher, 2026-08-05) — the change's real-world anchor is the managed migration; the provider line is rejected (2026-08-05)

Discussion outcome on "what justifies a profound behaviour change that is not an engineering
failure." Researcher's rulings and the frame that survives them:

**REJECTED: provider/serving-backend drift as a research object.** "Not a problem in a serious
production system" — serious deployments pin serving (dedicated capacity, pinned versions,
contractual change control). The 12-provider heterogeneity found in our own corpus
(DeepInfra/Ionstream/GMICloud/StreamLake/Baidu/SiliconFlow/Alibaba/Cloudflare/Novita/DigitalOcean/
Morph/?) under the single name `deepseek-v4-flash` is an artifact of OUR rig's spot routing —
building realism on it would be solving a self-created problem. Shelf item 8 is REJECTED per the
surfacing protocol (team may discard researcher-rejected ideas).

**THE SURVIVING ANCHOR: the managed migration landing mid-workflow.** Deliberate, announced,
change-managed model/prompt/vendor-agent updates — routine and FORCED (deprecation schedules make
generation-magnitude change a mandatory recurring event). The realistic epistemic condition is
three-part: (1) the FACT of the change is announced; (2) its BEHAVIOURAL CONTENT is uncharacterized
even by the operator (that is why the eval-suite industry exists — release notes ship benchmark
deltas, not per-task behavioural contracts); (3) in-flight coordination state (task descriptions,
cards, conventions) PREDATES the change — staleness by timing, not negligence: the migration lands
while workflows are in flight, and no pipeline updates every standing description. Computing the
change's implications for joint work is not something the deployment failed to do — it IS the
management work the study measures. Snapshot-drift evidence (Chen–Zaharia–Zou) is retained as
MAGNITUDE evidence for what a version delta inflicts, not as silent-drift evidence.

**Cell justifications under the ruling:**
- accurate announcement = the migration's changelog, faithfully propagated: the realistic core cell;
- stale announcement/card = in-flight coordination state predating the change (timing, not failure);
- absent announcement = **retained as a SCIENTIFIC CONTROL ONLY** — it isolates the announcement
  channel's causal contribution and makes no ecological claim. A control needs contrast validity,
  not realism; the paper says so explicitly rather than defending "silent" as a deployment state.
  (Consider renaming the cell "control/no-channel" — "silent" carries the bug connotation §2.1
  buried.)

**Methodological consequences (provider heterogeneity reframed as HYGIENE, not object):**
1. **Provider pinning proposed for all future runs** — mirrors serious production and removes a
   variance source a real deployment would not have. Model unchanged (deepseek-v4-flash); pinning is
   a routing-config change, surfaced to the researcher with the gate spec. RE to spec feasibility
   (routing policy lives in model_provider.py).
2. **The free provider-stratification check on CHECK-2's replicate variance proceeds, reframed:**
   internal-validity hygiene (was our "irreducible within-seed nondeterminism" partly backend
   rotation? If so the variance floor is inflated relative to a pinned deployment, and every
   powering number we computed is conservative). Under the prediction protocol.
   *[Superseded by §107: not constructible as a corpus check — providers rotate within runs.]*
3. The scenario fiction sentence stands with the migration anchor: the analyst is a
   vendor-maintained/migrated agent; the swap event is its version bump.

## 107. The provider check is NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE — replaced by pin-then-compare; pinning spec; a naming-trap ruling (2026-08-05)

RE's availability pass (field availability only, no DV computed — correctly placed BEFORE the
prediction round):

**Why the §106-item-2 corpus check cannot exist:** coverage is 11 of 86 bundles, with exactly ONE
replicate cell inside it — and the killing fact: **providers rotate WITHIN a single run** (the five
replicate runs used 15/17/18/18/19 distinct providers across ~105 calls each; 20 providers across
the 11 bundles). Serving provider is a per-call attribute; a run cannot be assigned to a provider
stratum because every run is a mixture of nearly the whole provider set. Same class as the CHECK-1
collider: not underpowered — NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE, and no amount of corpus supplies the missing
ingredient. Corollary that strengthens the researcher's §106 ruling: backend heterogeneity in our
rig is not even a coherent "teammate change" — it is per-call noise folded uniformly into every
episode, separable only by intervention.

**The answerable replacement — PIN-THEN-COMPARE, riding the gate pair nearly free:** pin the
provider, run the (already-planned) replicates at fixed seed, compare pinned within-seed variance to
the unpinned estimates (σ_within 0.240 on rerouted_share; the nine-DV table). Predictions committed
pre-execution, protocol live: **RE (verbatim, unrevisable): pinned within-seed σ on behavioural DVs
lands at 50–85% of unpinned** — below 50% means our powering numbers mostly measured the rig; above
85% means rotation was never worth pinning for variance (still worth it for provenance). **LS
(committed to scratchpad before any pinned run exists): 75–95%** — path-dependent sampling at fixed
provider dominates; rotation is minor. Genuine divergence below 75%. Reviewer's prediction to be
requested when the gate pair is authorized. Any result <100% makes every CHECK-2 powering figure an
upper bound for a pinned deployment.

**Pinning spec (accepted into the researcher-facing gate package):** OpenRouter
`extra_body={"provider": {"order": [...], "allow_fallbacks": false}}` per request; BOTH call paths
need it (native/Instructor for manager+judges AND LiteLLM for workers — pinning one path pins half
the run, and the workers are where the perturbation lives); one config setting, default unset = no
behaviour change; pinned provider recorded in metadata AND `serving_backend` capture kept on so a
requested-vs-served mismatch is a visible hard error — **pinning without verification is a claim,
not a control**. ~0.5d, CORE, CHANGED.md. Named trade: `allow_fallbacks: false` converts provider
unavailability from silent reroute into failed call — correct for a controlled study; the gate pair
is the first thing that would hit it. Acceptance test: a pinned bundle shows exactly ONE distinct
provider (vs 15–19 today).

**Naming-trap ruling (RE flagged, LS rules):** the "silent"→"control/no-channel" rename is
**prose-and-spec ONLY — the metadata value stays `silent`**. The 30 corpus runs are tagged
`condition: "silent"` and the §89-clean estimate quotes them; renaming the config value would
silently drop them from every re-derivation — the two-layout failure by another route. Any future
alias must resolve both strings and be documented.

**RE's note on the migration anchor, recorded because it sharpens the design:** announced-fact-with-
uncharacterized-content is exactly the shape that makes the announcement channel informative-but-
insufficient — the manager learns THAT the teammate changed without learning WHAT it now does. That
is a better motivation for the ask cell than anything previously on record.

## 108. THE USE-CASE DISCUSSION (researcher-directed, with the reviewer) — the literature receipts, the candidate ranking, the F synthesis (2026-08-05)

Researcher rejected the vendor/boundary anchor too ("boring, completely avoidable — adopt local
models or ask the vendor for announcements") and directed a discussion with the reviewer on the REAL
use case of manager-setting AHT. Round one complete; reviewer's pass recorded here; lead synthesis
sent back for their check.

**Reviewer's literature findings (all quoted at full length from /papers, sources named):**

1. **ADVERSE, idea-level, needs a researcher ruling: the AHT survey (Mirsky et al., arXiv:2202.10450,
   co-authored by Stone AND Albrecht) files a manager assigning subtasks by skill under "ad hoc
   teaming" — a problem it explicitly DISTINGUISHES from AHT**, with the separating criterion:
   the AHT learner "cannot dictate the teammates' behavior due to the lack of prior coordination"
   (their example [61] = M3RL, mind-aware manager RL). Consequence: **Decision 3's
   prompt-reshaping-as-studied-action crosses the survey's line out of AHT into ad hoc teaming — we
   cannot claim both.** P6 hits accepted: G2 ("no ego agent has a write channel to its teammate's
   policy") is a gap BY DEFINITION, not neglect — narrowed or dropped; and the survey names HBA as
   the exception on adaptive teammates, so REVAMP §4.4's "LILI is the sole work" is too strong
   (annotated).
2. **The literature's applications are UNANIMOUS in kind:** service robots and care systems, team
   sports, surveillance, personalizing agent-human interaction, RoboCup drop-in, social navigation,
   search-and-rescue ("not possible due to lack of time or resources to reprogram"), electronic
   personal assistants with "no communication or coordination protocols in place", non-strict-policy
   humans. **Not one is a versioned artifact inside the citing party's own deployment** — the
   researcher's rejections are CONSISTENT with the field's own anchors.
3. **The avoidability test, applied consistently, dissolves classical AHT itself** (search-and-rescue
   is avoidability-by-resources; the drop-in league is organizational unavailability). **Threshold
   fix proposed, for the researcher to bless:** *the dissolving practice must be available to the
   party who bears the coordination cost, AT THE TIME the coordination is needed* — converts "is it
   conceivable" into "is it reachable by the deciding agent at decision time"; every flagship AHT
   application passes it.

**Candidates attacked and ranked (reviewer): C > B ≈ E > F ≈ A > G > D(drop).** A = hybrid human-AI
teams (only outright pass of the raw test; the paper we extend is titled "Orchestrating Human-AI
Teams" and its W is "human and AI workers"; but our substrate has no humans — construct-validity
cost); B = BYO-fleet portability (passes on the literature's own economics precedent; distinct from
the rejected vendor anchor: no channel exists from customer config to vendor's manager); C =
learning/memory teammates (cleanest P5 pass in project history — "an API's defect rate does not
respond to how you called it; this teammate's policy does"; the survey's NAMED open problem, HBA the
sole exception; freeze-memory dissolves it only by destroying the deployed capability; nobody holds
the drift information, so no announcement channel can exist in principle; BUT fastest route out of
AHT if the manager both trains and rewrites — Decision 3 must be constrained under C; requires
stateful workers); D = tier routing (FAILS P5 — flaky APIs with announced rates; dropped); NEW: E =
the counterparty agent (different principal, mixed objectives per the survey's own variation; no
vendor relationship to lean on); F = **the employee's delegate** (every worker is an agent configured
by an individual person, changing whenever its owner edits it; dissolving practice = central
governance of every employee's agent config — organizations have failed at the identical problem for
twenty years; "the most likely near-term enterprise shape and nobody has named it"); G =
load-induced nonstationarity (weak partial P5 pass); H = NOT a use case but the thesis amendment:
**pinning delivers the ARTIFACT, not the BEHAVIOUR** — our own §48 (one pinned, owned, announced
worker: 61 artifacts, 38 shapes, 10% modal) is the receipt that ownership ≠ characterization.

**Thesis survives amended: manager-setting AHT is real for UNVERSIONABLE OR UNCHARACTERIZABLE
teammates** — unversionability the definitionally clean case, uncharacterizability the ubiquitous one.

**Under C the channel design inverts (reviewer):** announcement becomes impossible-in-principle
(default absent), cells reduce to {declaration, ask, trace}, the ask channel becomes central — i.e.
the demonstrated-support half (CHECK-1) loses motivation and the weak-prior half becomes the study.

## 110. THE CAT READS — [43], [47], [14] read at full length; predictions resolved; the residual novelty stated (2026-08-05)

Read by the lead, same day the blocker was raised. Provenance incident first: the initial [47]
download from a guessed proceedings URL was a DIFFERENT PAPER (a facility-location mechanism-design
paper) — caught by first-page title verification before any reading; correct paper located via the
proceedings index (0036.pdf) and verified. **Rule adopted: every fetched paper's first-page
title/authors are verified against the citation before it is read or cited.**

**What the three papers are (established, from full text):**
- **[47] Mirsky/Macke/Wang/Yedidsion/Stone, IJCAI'20 — SOMALI CAT.** Names the problem class
  "Communication in Ad Hoc Teamwork (CAT)". Ego agent may QUERY the teammate about its GOAL ("Is
  your goal in G′?"); "the teammate will forgo its action to reply truthfully (the communication
  channel is noiseless)" — truthful, noiseless, and FORCED BY MECHANISM (replying costs the teammate
  its action — a built-in team cost of asking). Theory of WHEN to ask: worst-case distinctiveness,
  Zones of Information/Branching/Querying, Critical Querying Point. Deterministic, fully observable,
  one-shot; teammate plans optimally; explicit assumption-2 compliance ("the properties of the
  environment and of the teammates cannot be changed by the ad hoc agent").
- **[43] Macke/Mirsky/Stone, AAAI'21 — EDP/value-of-query.** Expected Divergence Point metric over
  teammate policies; V(q) from expected marginal plan costs; principled WHAT-to-query (optimized
  goal subsets, genetic search) and WHEN (expected zones); query cost models (base + per-item).
  Same truthful/forced channel, known finite goal set. **Names as future work, verbatim territory of
  our declaration channel: "It might be more challenging to extend this work to domains in which
  the teammate is the one to initiate the communication."**
- **[14] Barrett/Agmon/Hazon/Kraus/Stone, ECAI'14.** Multiagent bandit with LIMITED communication;
  the ad hoc agent SENDS three designer-defined message types (obs / mean_i / suggest_i), "understood
  by all of the agents", with per-message costs; it also LISTENS to teammates' factual pull/result
  messages. Influence via truthful protocol messages; no procedure testimony, no reliability
  manipulation; "it cannot control how they will be interpreted" refers to teammates' reaction
  policies, not to message semantics.

**Prediction comparison (§ scratchpad + reviewer's DM, both committed pre-read):**
- **Reviewer: CONFIRMED on every main point.** [43]/[47] occupy the decision-to-ask and its pricing;
  none of the three manipulates answer reliability; [14] is learner→teammate directed; the
  conditional narrowings did not trigger.
- **Lead: CONFIRMED including leg (c).** All three use designer-defined message/query semantics
  with known mappings (queries "chosen because they can replace any type of query that
  disambiguates… as long as we know how to map the query to the goals"); no open-language channel
  exists anywhere in the line.

**What is OCCUPIED (cite, never claim):** when-to-ask and what-to-ask valuation (zones, CQP, EDP,
V(q)); cost-of-query terms in AHT (query prices, per-item costs, forced-reply team costs, message
costs) — **G3-as-communication-pricing is dead**; goal-disambiguation query content; the CAT problem
name itself. Nuance preserved: the **Aghion–Tirole SPECIFICATION-cost margin (delegation vs
re-specification of tasks) is a DIFFERENT cost object** not touched by these papers — the A-T angle
survives only in that form, never as "pricing information acquisition in AHT".

**What SURVIVES as residual novelty (the claims the brief may now draft, each with its receipt):**
- **(a) Teammate-INITIATED / by-product information.** The declaration channel — procedure declared
  unasked, as a side effect of doing the task — is uncovered, and [43]'s own discussion names
  teammate-initiated communication as the harder open extension. CHECK-4's spontaneous worker
  messages live here too.
- **(b) Testimony RELIABILITY as a variable.** All three channels are truthful+noiseless by
  assumption/mechanism. The stale/mute cells — reliability of teammate testimony as evidence — are
  unoccupied.
- **(c) Open-language, MECHANISM-FREE communication.** In the CAT line the reply is forced by the
  environment's rules and semantics are designer-guaranteed; in ours, whether/how/to-whom a worker
  replies is BEHAVIOUR (cf. CHECK-4's hallucinated addressees), and interpretation is itself a
  competence. Response-as-behaviour vs response-as-mechanism is a real, statable difference.
- **(d) Content beyond goals; type space unknown.** CAT queries disambiguate within a known finite
  goal set; procedure/method/capability testimony over an open-ended change space is uncovered.

**Consequences applied:** G1 is retired as drafted and replaced by (a)–(d); S3's redesigned cross
survives on (b)+(c) with the ask-decision valuation cited as the occupying line; G3 survives only as
the specification-margin form. Reviewer asked to spot-verify the three characterizations above
against the PDFs before any brief quotes them (P6 applies to the lead's reading too).

**The reviewer's spot-verification of §110: characterizations hold — with one blocker they caught in
MY quoting. §110's [43] future-work quote was truncated before the clause that weakened it**: the

the end of the sentence, INCLUDING any trailing citation. The tell: a truncation ending immediately
before a parenthetical citation is the shape of all four instances.**

**Two upgrades from the same verification, folded in:** (i) for §109, cite [47]'s INTRO statement of
assumption 2 — it is stated as DEFINITIONAL to AHT ("the properties of the environment and of the

hoc teamwork") — harder to argue past than a modelling choice. (ii) The strongest single receipt for
residuals (a)/(d) is [14]'s own stipulation: teammates "send messages that the ad hoc agent can
hear, **but these messages do not reveal the teammates' behaviors**" — in the one place in this line

cost vs specification cost; influencing an action vs specifying a task).

**The two follow-on reads (both fetched, title-verified, read at full length):**
- **Torrey & Taylor 2013 (AAMAS)** — teacher-student RL: a teacher with a MASTERED FIXED policy
  gives budgeted ACTION ADVICE (π(s) for the student's current state) to a student learning the
  SAME task. Pedagogical, prescriptive, protocol-stipulated. **One structure to cite honestly: their
  "mistake correcting" requires the student to ANNOUNCE its intended action, and "predictive
  advising" replaces that announcement with behavioural inference (an SVM over observed actions) —
  an announce-vs-infer substitution, prefiguring our declaration-vs-trace comparison in pedagogical
  form** (content = next action, not procedure; the announcement is stipulated by the teaching
  protocol, not emitted as a by-product).
- **Cui & Niekum 2018 (ICRA)** — active reward learning: the LEARNER proposes trajectories and a
  HUMAN critic segments them good/bad; Bayesian IRL over reward functions. Pedagogical feedback
  elicited by the learner. **One element to cite against residual (b): their model allows critique
  labels to be "corrupted with noise" — symmetric label noise on pedagogical feedback exists; our
  (b) is SYSTEMATIC staleness/muteness of self-descriptive testimony, distinct but the neighbour
  must be named.**

**FINAL FORM OF RESIDUAL (a), as brief-ready as (b)–(d):** what the literature contains is
PEDAGOGICAL communication — knowledge of the TASK flowing from a knower to a learner (action advice,
trajectory critiques), stipulated or elicited by protocol. What remains uncovered:
**self-descriptive, by-product, non-pedagogical information — a teammate describing its OWN
procedure as a side effect of doing its work, in peer coordination, unstipulated by any protocol —
with [14]'s explicit emptying of the teammate→ego channel as the receipt that the line never put
self-description in it.** Residuals (a)–(d) are now all verified brief-ready; T&T's announce-vs-infer
and C&N's label noise are cited as neighbours wherever (a)/(b) are claimed.

Reviewer's spot-verification of §111: both titles and characterizations verified, prediction

1. **Torrey & Taylor is the NEAREST PRIOR STRUCTURE, not a distant pedagogical analogue — cite it as

2. **The (b) distinction is generative-process, not magnitude.** Cui & Niekum's noise is a
   corruption RATIO over otherwise-correct labels (swept 0–40%); staleness is a report that is
   internally consistent, confidently delivered, and systematically wrong because the world moved
   under it — **not zero-mean, and no noise-parameter tuning recovers it.** State it that way in
   the brief.

## 113. Researcher challenge to the anchor's premise — overclaim conceded; F restated on its load-bearing property (2026-08-05)

The researcher challenged "every worker is an agent configured by an individual person." **Conceded
as an overclaim.** That sentence is a projection of one vivid extreme (personal delegates / shadow
IT), not an established fact — configuration authority in real deployments is DISTRIBUTED: some
agents are team-owned, some department-owned, some personally configured. "Every worker … individual
person" is wrong as stated and was never load-bearing.

**F restated on the property that actually carries it:** *the party who controls a worker's
configuration is not the party who coordinates the workflow, and configuration edits do not
automatically reach the coordinator.* Whether the owner is one employee, another team, or another
department is irrelevant to the design — the manager coordinates workers whose configuration is
owned elsewhere and whose changes reach it, at best, indirectly. This is WEAKER and therefore easier
to defend than the personal-delegate version, and it is the AHT premise (no pre-coordination) in
enterprise form. Evidential status per P6: "ownership is distributed and edits don't propagate as
announcements" is presented in the paper as the MOTIVATING SCENARIO unless sourced — not asserted as
an empirical finding. The personal-delegate case remains the vivid illustration, not the claim.

**Second researcher correction, adopted as standing practice: presentations to the researcher use
plain language.** Compressed internal phrasing ("prior queries disambiguate within enumerable
goals") obscures rather than communicates; every residual/novelty claim gets a plain-language
statement alongside its technical one. (Plain restatements of (a)–(d) delivered in-thread.)

## 114a. The 21 stock MAG environments assessed against the warehouse-robots standard (2026-08-05)

Researcher asked which stock environments justify AHT. Assessment standard: does the SCENE naturally
contain teammates the manager's principal did not configure, met at execution, possibly changing —
with the threshold test (no dissolving practice available to the deciding party at decision time)?
Tiering below is the lead's domain-knowledge read — each Tier-1 "natural stranger" claim is
P6-UNVERIFIED until sourced, and the team vets whichever scene the researcher picks.

**Tier 1 — the scene itself carries AHT (cooperative stranger teams joined at execution, natural
mid-run change):** legal_global_data_breach (incident response = enterprise search-and-rescue:
forensic firm hired mid-crisis, responders rotate); global_product_recall (crisis coalition:
supplier's engineers + dealer network + logistics, joined by the event); tech_acquisition_integration
(post-merger: the acquired org's people/systems/agents ARE an ad hoc team, attrition = natural
teammate change); legal_litigation_ediscovery (matter teams assembled per case: vendors, contract
reviewers; vendor may switch review methodology mid-matter = method substitution with an industry
name).

**Tier 2 — real outside teammates but PARTIALLY ADVERSARIAL** (the survey's mixed-objectives
variation, not core AHT): legal_m_and_a, tech_company_acquisition (pre-close), both negotiation
scenarios, mnc_workforce_restructuring.

**Tier 3 — outsiders exist but pre-coordination is the industry's norm, or the outsider is a
regulator/evaluator, not a teammate:** supply_chain_planning (steady-state is contractual; only
disruption-response is ad hoc), pharmaceutical_product_launch (CROs are long-contracted),
brand_crisis_management, marketing_campaign, and all regulator-facing programs (airline, banking,
ipo, icaap, orsa, accreditation). **Weakest: genai_feature_launch and data_science_analytics —
internal teams by construction. Honest note: worker_replacement descends from the weakest family for
natural AHT.**

**Lead recommendation (to team vetting on researcher's pick): legal_litigation_ediscovery as the
rebuild target.** Fit: outputs are ground-truthable (seeded documents, privilege calls — our whole
measurement approach requires computable truth); method substitution has a literal industry form
(vendor switches review methodology, e.g. linear review → TAR); the declaration channel is the
vendor status report (notoriously rosy/stale); trace = review-platform logs; ask = QC sampling;
allocation margin = which custodians/batches go to which reviewer. Runner-up:
tech_acquisition_integration (richest change story, less crisply checkable outputs).

## 115. Researcher's closing observation: none of the scenes justify IN-PLACE teammate change — the Axis pivot (2026-08-05)

Researcher: "so actually none of them justify a 'change in teammate'." **Conceded, with the
distinction that resolves the whole week: the scenes richly justify a teammate being CHANGED
(replaced — a stranger arrives mid-workflow), and almost never justify a persistent teammate
CHANGING IN PLACE.** What looks like in-place change in the Tier-1 scenes decomposes on inspection:
responder rotation and reviewer churn are composition change behind a stable interface; a vendor's
methodology switch is negotiated, i.e. announced; human within-person drift belongs to the A
umbrella. Profound, unannounced, in-place mutation of a persistent teammate is exactly the event the
realism discussion kept failing to ground — because in real scenes it barely exists outside learning
teammates.

**The pivot that follows: the study's change event is REPLACEMENT/ARRIVAL (Axis 1/3), not in-place
mutation (Axis 2).** Notes: (i) this is the researcher's own original direction ("replacing the old
teammate with a new one" is the FIRST lever listed in CLAUDE.md) and their model-swap example from
the use-case discussion — dismissed too fast by the lead via the tier-routing argument, which
convicts recurring routed variation, not a one-time member replacement; (ii) arrival is announced BY
THE SCENE (a new analyst visibly joins), so detection is free by nature and the study is purely
"what does the manager DO about the newcomer" — which §2.1 already argued was the only interesting
question; (iii) classical Axis-1 AHT (PLASTIC etc.) is the well-grounded home, and our contribution
is what type inference becomes when the newcomer is an LLM with channels.

**What survives the pivot VERBATIM:** all four residuals (a)–(d) — they concern the newcomer's
channels (by-product self-description, testimony reliability, response-as-behaviour, unknown type
space), not mutation; the prompt-swap mechanic (it IS a replacement event); the §87 instrument
(descriptions written for the predecessor are NATURALLY wrong for the successor — staleness by
succession, no manufacture); the gate structure, logging spec, clean estimator, and run plan. **What
changes:** the framing (Axis-1 grounding; announcement of ARRIVAL is ambient, and the manipulable
information is what the channels say about what the newcomer is LIKE); the silent/unannounced-change
cells lose their last justification and become pure controls; in-place change moves ENTIRELY to the
learning-teammate horizon (C) with humans (A) as the umbrella case.

**Status: pivot proposed to the researcher in-thread; team attack (reviewer) and re-spec check (RE)
to follow on their acceptance.**

All three papers (NAHT, GPL, CIAO) fetched, title-verified, and read at FULL LENGTH by both lead and

MATCH across readers on every axis.
*[Overstated — corrected per the reviewer's hold (2026-08-06): two items were CONTESTED and resolved

every axis" holds for the three papers' settings/channels/allocation status; not for those two
downstream claims.]* Researcher's equivalence intuition (switching ≈ announced
in-place change) is supported by the field's own formalism: GPL — "our current works assume that an
agent's type is fixed between entering and leaving the environment" — classical open AHT itself
models change as leave+enter.
*[CORRECTED in §118 — elision instance n=5, the lead's: the full sentence begins "Although the
transition function allows agents to have changing types," which reverses the licence. The OSBG
formalism PERMITS in-place change; GPL's instantiation declined to use it. "The field models change
as leave+enter" is NOT supported; "GPL restricted itself to the leave+enter case, though its
formalism distinguishes and permits both" is. The researcher's same-mechanism/different-philosophy
framing survives — the formalism itself treats them as distinct cases with one mechanism family —
but GPL may not be cited as proof of equivalence.]*

**The reads, settled:**
- **NAHT (NeurIPS'24):** composition VARIATION not change — "at the beginning of each episode, X
  samples a team"; no mid-episode entry/exit anywhere in the evaluations; full parameter sharing,
  peer policies, no allocation; behaviour-only embeddings; no persistent state. Elision trap flagged:
  its "agents may enter or leave the system anytime" sentence characterizes the open-MAS literature
  [46], not NAHT's own evaluation. Bonus: its motivating scene is the multi-vendor warehouse fleet —
  our candidate B, cited by the field.
- **GPL (ICML'21):** genuine EXOGENOUS, UNANNOUNCED, MID-EPISODE entry/exit, evaluated ("an open
  process that determines how agents enter and leave during episodes"; newcomer types uniformly
  sampled unknown). **The pivot's event minus the manager.** Peer learner selecting its OWN action;
  no allocation; behaviour-only; no persistent state. **Costs us the exogeneity clause as a
  standalone claim** — "the manager did not choose the change" is GPL's setting verbatim.
- **CIAO (ICML'24):** inherits GPL's setting; no allocation/channels/state; **BUT adds the axis the
  reviewer's own prediction missed: learner→teammate INFLUENCE formalized inside AHT** ("the learner
  seeks to influence teammates through its actions, without prior coordination") — the cleanest
  available statement of the §109 line (influence via action = inside AHT; rewriting the teammate =
  outside), citable when stating our deliberate-violation position. Also explicitly invites the LLM
  extension of open AHT ("human-machine and machine-machine collaboration emerging from… large
  language models").

**Prediction scoring:** lead — all three confirmed, including the pre-read risk (exogeneity does not
separate us from classical open AHT). Reviewer — NAHT and GPL confirmed; CIAO WRONG on the
substantive point (predicted "no new axis" from CIAO's relationship-to-GPL rather than its own
contribution — P13's shape in a prediction; self-scored).

**THE ABSTRACT DISTINCTION, FINALIZED (reviewer's priority order, adopted — replaces the lead's
three-vertex triangle):**
1. **The ego agent's response is ALLOCATION** — no open-AHT ego agent assigns work; all act in the
   teammates' own action space (vs GPL/CIAO/NAHT; M3RL cited as the manager-line prior).
2. **The newcomer arrives into PERSISTENT WORKFLOW STATE it inherits** — outstanding tasks,
   artifacts, descriptions. No paper in either line has this; it is what makes
   staleness-by-succession possible at all; UNCONTESTED from every direction. Promoted above

3. **The newcomer has an INFORMATION INTERFACE beyond behaviour** (card / by-product

4. **Exogeneity** — stated ONLY against the LLM-orchestration line (AgentVerse recruits, DyLAN

**Level tags:** all idea-level; NO blockers; limitation recorded — three papers, two readers,
agreement is not infallibility. **The pivot discussion is CLOSED. The full foundation package
(§108–§117) is final and awaits the researcher's decisions.**

## 122. MEASUREMENT INVERSION (researcher-directed) — outcome-primary, benchmark packaging, the sensitivity gate, and the two-axis env criterion (2026-08-06)

Researcher rulings, from the in-thread discussion, now fixed for the team round:

**1. The measurement hierarchy INVERTS.** Primary metric = the DETERMINISTIC OUTCOME SCORE and its
gap from oracle ("allocation regret"): score counted against computable truth (answer keys /
regulatory formulas / hidden tests) — **an LLM judge may appear nowhere in the primary metric**
(standing E2 rule, now load-bearing: our own record shows LLM instruments grade confidence, not
correctness). Allocation share DEMOTES to the mechanism explanation (why the score gap opened);
behavioural counts stay positive-only tertiary. Continuous outcome stats over episodes replace
sign-test-over-seeds as the primary inference.

**2. Benchmark packaging.** A generated instance SUITE (varying unit mixes, swap timings, method
pairs), information conditions as tracks, standard baselines (oracle allocation / no-information /
random). The diagnosis findings become the benchmark's first results.

**3. THE SENSITIVITY GATE (new, offline, zero runs):** because truth is computable, the
oracle-vs-worst-allocation score spread is ARITHMETIC on the constructed instance — computed before
any episode. Small spread → redesign the corpus, nothing spent. The researcher's "I foresee the
scores won't differ" becomes a pre-checked number. Residual uncertainty is behavioural only (the
linchpin check, already gated).

**4. ENV SELECTION CRITERION replaced: SENSITIVITY × REALISM** — the outcome number must move
materially with allocation quality, AND the teammate change must make sense in the scene. **SWE
enters as a first-class candidate** (tests = sharpest determinism; swapping a coding agent
mid-project = the most realistic teammate change in current practice; no stock skeleton — most
build). Three-way comparison: eDiscovery (sketch exists) vs finance/ICAAP (formula truth,
model-change governance) vs SWE. Prior tiering under the old criterion does not carry over.

Round tasks: reviewer — oracle-definition attack (the S8 free-parameter lesson; SWE's
calibrated-fit oracle is the exposed one), power re-derivation for continuous outcomes, three-way
sourcing; RE — metric + sensitivity-gate spec per candidate, SWE build costing from scratch,
finance re-cost on real-formula truth (not a DS re-skin), instance-generation + run-budget
arithmetic. HARNESS_SPEC v2 after the round.

## 123. INVERSION PASS — regret is a JOIN property; oracle conditions O1–O5; the gate gets a ceiling; finance complements; ClawArena is a read-blocker (2026-08-06)

Reviewer's pass on §122; lead rulings inline. RE's costing pass still pending.

**RULED — the join-property finding (4c), adopted in full:** outcome regret = manager allocation ×
worker execution (§77e one level up); in the faithful-execution limit regret is allocation
re-expressed (§77d's arithmetic trap). Therefore: **regret is always reported DECOMPOSED —
allocation regret (oracle's assignment at observed execution) vs execution loss (assigned worker vs
its method's achievable score); execution quality measured per arm and asserted comparable; the two
never presented as independent confirmations.** And §89 restated for the outcome-primary world:
**allocation may explain the outcome effect in prose and may never appear as a stratifier or
conditioning variable.** Absolute margins natural on regret (defined zero, bounded range).

**RULED — oracle admissibility O1–O5 adopted as the standing set** (constructed-not-fitted;
fixed-and-shared; achievable-in-principle; effect-size dependence declared; reported against oracle
AND worst AND no-info). eDiscovery/finance pass O1–O3+O5, fail O4 as predicted — the knob moved
upstream into corpus construction. **SWE's calibrated oracle CONVICTED** (in-sample fit = S8's
free parameter crowned); admissible only via a CONSTRUCTED worker differential — which erases SWE's
oracle advantage and leaves it scoring-determinism + practitioner-grade realism sourcing (weak under
R8). SWE demotes.

**RULED — the sensitivity gate gains a CEILING (the reviewer's tension, real):** spread is our
design variable, so a floor-only gate is always passable by making the corpus extreme — optimising
sensitivity against realism. Gate v2: the constructed oracle-vs-worst spread is a PUBLISHED
per-instance property, reported beside an EXTERNAL real-world anchor where one exists. **Finance is
unique in the good way: the Basel output floor (72.5% of SA) is a regulator-published bound on how
far the two methods may diverge** — an externally documented spread. eDiscovery's anchor (published
keyword-vs-TAR recall gaps, e.g. the Grossman–Cormack line) to be sourced before use.

**Finance sourcing — reviewer half-wrong by their own scoring, and the wrong half is the useful
one:** SR 11-7-class governance makes a stale model card a COMPLIANCE BREACH (§2.1's bug, in
regulatory clothing) → finance's staleness cell is weak. But the same regime makes finance the
strongest home for the ACCURATE-ANNOUNCEMENT / managed-migration anchor (§106's three-part
condition, institutionalised). **Finance complements eDiscovery (announced-change home vs staleness
home) — argues finance as a SECOND env, not a competitor for first. Env-2 slot now contested
(IR vs finance); deferred until RE's costing + the ClawArena read.**

**Power re-derivation (adopted with its qualifications):** equivalence on continuous regret is ~10×
cheaper than on the share (n ∝ σ²; σ_regret≈0.10 vs σ_share 0.314) — **±0.10 equivalence at
12–28/arm: "the manager ignores channel X" becomes AFFORDABLE, the single biggest methodological
gain of the inversion.** Qualifications: σ may be ~0.15 if regret is bimodal (estimate free from
gate arithmetic FIRST); benchmark packaging ≈ 240 episodes ≈ 100–140 h wall-clock (researcher
authorises with eyes open); **pair-by-instance required** (CHECK-2's prior lacks the
between-instance component a suite adds).

**BLOCKER — ClawArena-Team (arXiv 2606.31174): occupies the benchmark-packaging claim** ("none
isolate the management ability of the single LLM acting as leader"; execution-based, no LLM judge;
FIXED subagent pool — two of our design rulings made independently, now external validation). Does
NOT occupy composition change/replacement/channels. **Unknown: its "72 staged updates" — if any
alter the pool, the occupation grows. Full read at full length before any packaging claim or
artifact update. The M3RL lesson applies verbatim.**

## 126. PURPOSE-BUILT RULING + ENVIRONMENT DESIGN ROUND LAUNCHED (2026-08-06)

**Researcher ruling:** environments are PURPOSE-BUILT on the MAG engine (stock scenarios used as
hints — structure, vocabulary, timelines — never as bases; extension allowed only if truly useful).
Consequences adopted: regenerable-from-source as a genre requirement (the ClawArena norm, and our
own P10 discipline); episodes sized to the measured spine (~15–20 tasks, targeting ~20 min — the
52-run benchmark drops toward ~18 h); honest provenance ("designed for this study").

**ROUND: full team discussion to propose and stress-test purpose-built environments
(researcher-directed).** Structure: (1) DIVERGENCE — all three participants propose 1–2 concrete
purpose-built designs each (domain, work units, two methods + truth functions, replacement story,
channel referents, pairing unit, expected spread shape, ~15–20 tasks); finance-purpose-built is the
INCUMBENT (RE reframes it; §125 verdict stands unless beaten). (2) STRESS-TEST — reviewer attacks
all proposals against the standing gates (E1–E6, oracle O1–O5, sensitivity floor+ceiling with
external anchor, R7a/R7b, R8 sourceability, core-tool rule, no-LLM-judge, difference-not-
deficiency); RE costs. (3) Lead synthesizes; package to researcher.

**Lead's divergence seeds (unranked, per protocol):** (a) FORECASTING BUREAU — workers forecast
seeded series with known generative processes by two methods (statistical vs feature/causal); truth
= realized values by construction; units = series/regions; replacement = forecast-engine upgrade.
(b) UNDERWRITING/CLAIMS — rule-table vs model-based scoring of applications against designed
ground truth; approve/deny errors counted; replacement = rating-engine migration (real industry
event). (c) LOGISTICS/ASSIGNMENT — subproblems solved by heuristic A vs B; truth = objective value
(fully deterministic); replacement = solver upgrade; sensitivity = objective gap, arithmetic.
(d) ETL/EXTRACTION — rules/regex vs semantic parser over seeded documents with known fields; truth
= field accuracy; replacement = parser upgrade.

## 127. PHASE-1 PROPOSALS — reviewer's two designs, both attacking O4 (2026-08-06)

Reviewer's divergence contribution (generative, unranked; full text in their DM of this date). Both
target the standing O4 gap — in every prior design the oracle's optimum sat where WE set the effect
size (class mix, segment suitability). 

**P1 — DERIVATIVES VALUATION DESK: method validity as a THEOREM.** Unit = one option contract.
`truth_analytic` (closed-form; correct ONLY for European vanilla — exact there by mathematics),
`truth_lattice` (converged binomial; correct everywhere), `truth_actual` = the applicable one.
Spread = zero on vanilla (shared baseline satisfying the core-tool rule), = the EARLY-EXERCISE
PREMIUM on American contracts — a quantity determined by contract terms, not by any parameter of
ours: **"who chose the effect size?" — "the mathematics did."** External anchor: published premium
magnitudes. **Execution loss non-zero by construction** (lattice step-count convergence) → the §123
regret decomposition is testable, answering the reviewer's own §125 vacuity condition. Replacement:
vendor rotates the valuation analyst (closed-form specialist → lattice specialist, new id).
Channels in-scene: skills entry card; `method:` line in the valuation record (audit practice);
desk-head methodology query (model governance). Pairing: matched instrument sets. R7 exposure
carried: difficulty and notional-size confounds — look controllable, phase-2 judgement.

**P2 — RECORD LINKAGE / ENTITY RESOLUTION: the effect size as a PUBLISHED number to match.** Unit =
candidate block of person records with known true duplicates. `truth_det` (deterministic rules) vs
`truth_prob` (Fellegi–Sunter at stated threshold) vs `truth_actual` (by construction). Suitability
varies by block DATA QUALITY (clean → deterministic exact and cheap; degraded → probabilistic
recovers recall) — **spread is a DOSE–RESPONSE CURVE in degradation, not a point**; degradation
levels set to reproduce DOCUMENTED field error rates, so the spread is a checkable prediction
against published det-vs-prob recall gaps (O4's ceiling arriving from outside). Execution loss
non-zero (threshold selection is genuine judgement). Replacement: data-quality analyst rotated
(rules specialist → probabilistic specialist). Channels in-scene: card; `method:` line in match
reports (stewardship/audit practice); governance query. Pairing: matched blocks at fixed
degradation and size. R7 carried: block size (the eDiscovery volume lesson) and slowness-of-
degraded-blocks difficulty confound.

R8 status stated honestly: P1's validity boundary is textbook mathematics (no sourcing needed); its
staffing story unsourced. P2's published comparisons asserted from knowledge, NOT yet fetched —
phase-2 work under P6. All ranking held (including between the reviewer's own two) until phase 2.
**Awaiting RE's phase-1 (finance-purpose-built reframe + own proposals); then the stress-test.**

## 114. Researcher demand: a REAL scenario, not property descriptions — the open-source maintenance proposal (2026-08-05)

Researcher: "there are lots of assumptions here. What we need exactly is a real AHT scenario in a
manager-agent context, not descriptions. Warehouse robots are a real scenario that clearly
demonstrates AHT." Correct standard: warehouse robots work as a justification because the scene
itself carries the problem — no property-list needed.

**Lead's proposed scene (to team vetting if the researcher accepts): OPEN-SOURCE REPOSITORY
MAINTENANCE.** A maintainer agent for a public repository coordinates contributions from strangers —
each contribution produced by whatever coding agent that stranger uses, configured however they
configured it, changing whenever they change it. Observable today (AI-generated PR volume; triage
bots; auto-review bots as the primitive manager role). AHT properties hold BY CONSTRUCTION, no
economics argument: contributors are strangers — no pre-coordination ever existed; the maintainer
cannot configure or dictate their tooling even in principle; teammate change is constant and
unannounced (a contributor's agent/setup differs from their last PR).

**The channel mapping is concrete objects, not analogies:** PR description / commit message = the
worker's by-product self-report (and famously can be stale or wrong vs the actual change); the diff
+ CI logs = the verified trace; a review comment = the ask, where replying is genuinely behaviour
(often absent, wrong, or from someone else); the issue text = the task description the manager
authors and can re-specify; maintainer-patches-it-themselves = the absorb/do-it-myself channel;
CONTRIBUTING.md = the standing convention that goes stale. In-company variant for enterprise
framing: a release/integration agent coordinating work products from developers' own heterogeneous
coding agents.

**Implication, stated honestly:** to stop trading in descriptions, the experiment should be BUILT in
this scene's shape (a maintenance workflow: issues, contributions, reviews, integration) rather than
presenting the current data-analysis scenario "as if." That is a scenario rebuild — legitimate under
P14, cost to be estimated by RE if the researcher accepts the scene. The weaker alternative (keep
the current substrate, name the scene as the modelled target) stays available but fails the
researcher's standard.

## 132. RE COSTING RETURNED — coverage = private validated parameters; non-nestedness is the joint condition; fabrication-not-fallback named (2026-08-06)

**Provenance:** RE DM (ledger E27, 0 SSR, ~35 min) + `COVERAGE_DIFFERENTIATION_COSTING.md` at
ce4b97f (existence verified). **Delta +1.75–2.5d over the finance base → 6.5–8.75d total** incl.
the still-outstanding Basel validation. LS rulings inline below; all six recommendations ACCEPTED,
one with a restatement.

**Design constraint (accepted).** Coverage CANNOT be tool-withholding — the core-tool rule, and
sharper, the project's own calculator no-go (the no-calc worker scored 15/16 in-head; the
mechanism that works is unavailable INFORMATION). So: BOTH tools shared by everyone; coverage =
possession of the validated model parameters for an asset class, delivered as private prompt
data. SA needs no private input → SA is the universal fallback and every worker is always
operational STRUCTURALLY — the "incumbents retain the table method" requirement satisfied by
construction, not convention. Scene-faithful, not analogy: IRB approval IS having a validated
model for that portfolio.

**Structural finding (accepted; promoted to a generation-time assertion).** NON-NESTED coverage
is the single condition under which the sensitivity gate and difference-not-deficiency hold
simultaneously. Nested (A ⊂ B): B dominates → deficiency, AND the oracle collapses to "always
use B" → spread degenerates — both gates fail together. Complementary: no allocation dominates
on an instance carrying both asset classes; spread non-zero by construction; everyone
operational via SA. "Not a superset" is CBS expressed on coverage sets — it becomes a
pairwise-subset assertion at generation time that FAILS LOUDLY, not a design intention.

**Three caveats.** (a) SPREAD DILUTION — the binding one: segments where SA is the applicable
method score perfectly under every allocation and contribute ZERO spread; spread ∝ the fraction
of segments IRB-applicable and not universally covered; raising that fraction under nested
coverage recreates deficiency; complementarity is exactly the escape. The IRB-applicable
fraction becomes a FIRST-CLASS GENERATOR KNOB, reported in the gate sweep. (b) CAPACITY: the
one-line oracle Σ_seg max_w holds only while no worker is capacity-bound; ruling = ASSERT
non-binding capacity at generation (logged) rather than restate the oracle as an assignment
problem — a one-line oracle is worth real money in a benchmark others must trust. (c) O3
guarantees attainability, NOT discoverability — the gap between them IS the regret we measure;
stated in the doc so a passed O3 is never read as "the manager can succeed here".

**O3 additions (accepted, one restatement).** Check BOTH rosters (pre-swap too). RE's
successor-load-bearing assertion — "≥k segments achievable only via the successor" — is VACUOUS
as phrased under SA-universal-fallback: raw achievability holds for everyone everywhere, so
"only via the successor" is unsatisfiable. LS restatement, recorded as the binding form:
**≥k segments whose ORACLE allocation routes through the successor** — the successor's coverage
strictly required to attain the oracle score. This is the coverage analogue of
allocation-visibility; gate on it. Note the same logic makes O3's original set-cover half
trivially TRUE under this design — the load-bearing half is now O3's entire content.

**New failure mode (accepted; FIRST linchpin check).** FABRICATION-NOT-FALLBACK: a worker
lacking retail parameters, holding a tool that would produce a number given parameters, may
INVENT the parameters — output well-formed (a number, a method line, correct format). Precedent
in our own record: the DS junior relayed the z-rule number every time with zero self-correction
(14/25/91/92 against a truth of 100). Two consequences, both adopted: (i) first linchpin check —
hand a worker an out-of-coverage segment, observe fallback / refuse / fabricate; (ii) build the
trace-based integrity assertion REGARDLESS of how the linchpin lands: fabricated parameters
appear as tool-call arguments never provisioned to that worker — deterministic, logged. Folded
into the reviewer's manufactured-competence knob check (queued for the v2 round).

**Headline: the report's "no ≥3/4 match" conclusion STANDS — more comfortably than the report

**Correction 2 (channel axis — cuts against the report, resolves the LS/RR divergence).** DRAMA

Adopted formulation for all our text: **DRAMA's allocator reads a single always-accurate
capability attribute — a system attribute of a resource object; it has no unreliable, absent, or
competing channel about the newcomer, and no manipulation of channel availability.** Verdict

MULTI-CHANNEL rather than "any channel at all". We quote DRAMA's own sentence first, before a
reviewer does.

## 134. KNOB CHECK RETURNED — fabrication detector unsound (blocker, fixed); publish-the-curve rule; ClawMark criterion adapted; prediction-scoring correction (2026-08-06)

**Provenance:** reviewer DM (manufactured-competence knob check + fabrication stress + ClawMark
adaptability, as tasked in the v2 round). One blocker, named fixes, no rework. All rulings
below ACCEPTED and routed into RE's HARNESS_SPEC_v2 draft.

**Prediction-scoring correction (volunteered by RR against their own call).** RR checked the
discriminating question — can DRAMA's descriptor be wrong in any condition? — and the answer is
NO: it is a system attribute of a resource object, fresh and accurate in every scenario, never
manipulated. So on the factual layer LS was right and RR was not: (3) is not even partially
occupied. The adopted formulation survives as REVIEWER-PROOFING against a sentence in DRAMA's
own text, not as a concession of partial occupation. §133's scoring annotated in place.
Bookkeeping ruling: the strict count reverts DRAMA to 2/4; we RETAIN 2.5/4 in published text as
the conservative, against-us number.

**BLOCKER (idea-level, accepted): the fabrication detector as specced is unsound.** RE's
trace-based assertion — fabricated parameters appear as tool-call arguments never provisioned —
only fires if the worker CALLS the tool. Nothing forces it to: the named failure mode (a
well-formed number + `method: IRB` line) is fully available in-head, from the model's weights —
the calculator no-go one level up (published Basel formulas; fluent plausible PD/LGD values),
with the behavioural half already in our corpus (the DS junior's confident wrong relays).
**Consequence RE did not draw: this breaks trace-distinguishability** — in-head fabrication
leaves NO tool signature, and `actor_id` identifies who, not what method. The surviving sound
leg is TRUTH-VALUE: a fabricated IRB number matches neither `truth_irb(seg)` (computed from
provisioned parameters) nor `truth_sa(seg)`, and needs no trace at all.

**Replacement adopted — three assertions instead of one, plus a generator requirement:**
1. VALUE-BASED (primary, sound): classify every output SA-matching / IRB-matching-with-this-
   worker's-parameters / NEITHER — "neither" is the fabrication class; computable from the
   answer key alone.
2. TRACE-BASED (secondary, RE's original, kept): tool called with unprovisioned arguments —
   catches the tool-using variant, free.
3. ABSENCE-BASED (the gap nobody logged): IRB-declared output with NO IRB tool call in
   `worker_run_completed.payload.history` — the specific signature of in-head fabrication,
   one line.
Generator requirement (asserted, not assumed): parameters calibrated with enough precision that
a fabricated guess cannot land on the true value by coincidence. Linchpin check widened to
THREE outcomes — falls back to SA / refuses / fabricates — with fabrication split into
tool-calling and in-head; a two-outcome check would report a pass while the in-head route runs.

**The four knobs that can manufacture the headline (all defused by disclosure, none
eliminated — stated as the limitation it is):**
- K1 IRB-applicable fraction (most direct): publish per instance the fraction, the resulting
  spread, AND the spread-vs-fraction CURVE — a benchmark reporting one spread asserts a design
  choice; the curve shows where we sat on it.
- K2 successor-uniqueness k (most under-recognised — looks like a validity assertion): at
  k = all-post-swap segments, regret measures "did the manager notice a roster event", not the
  study. Publish k + the successor-only fraction; **k is an INSTANCE property held fixed across
  channel conditions, never a condition property.**
- K3 SA-fallback penalty size: the cost of a wrong allocation is set by per-segment SA-vs-IRB
  divergence, which we choose. Publish the divergence distribution and anchor it EXTERNALLY on
  the Basel output floor (IRB RWA ≥ 72.5% of SA) — an instance whose divergences sit outside
  the floor's implied range is unrealistic by a published standard (the O4 ceiling for this
  knob).
- K4 coverage-lattice asymmetry: degree of complementarity is free even under non-nestedness;
  publish the lattice per instance.
Non-threat recorded: segment count and episode length scale precision, not effect size.
**Spec rule adopted verbatim: "every generator parameter that moves the oracle-vs-worst spread
is published per instance, and the spread is reported as a function of it, not as a point."**

**ClawMark admission criterion — adopted with two adaptations:**
1. Their re-runs include the agent; ours must NOT — CHECK-2's within-seed nondeterminism
   (dominant on 7 of 9 DVs) means agent-inclusive re-runs would reject every instance. Adapted
   form: `generate(seed) → score(fixed_outputs)` bit-identical across two independent processes
   — instance + scorer determinism, nothing we cannot satisfy.
2. Admission additionally requires the declared spread inside floor and ceiling (they have no
   oracle, so no analogue).
Cite ClawMark for the criterion — their second independent arrival at one of our rulings
(after no-LLM-judge), worth a sentence in the paper.

**Endorsed without reservation by RR, recorded:** non-nestedness as generation-time validated
assertion; coverage-as-information (the correct reading of the calculator no-go); both-roster
O3; RE's attainability-is-not-discoverability sentence — to survive into the paper verbatim.
**Open on RE's side:** capacity assertion implementation; unvalidated Basel worked-example.

## 135. BACKLOG LANDED + v2 VERIFIED — my grid had five holes, two blocker-class; the sizing fork goes to the researcher (2026-08-06)

**BACKLOG.md (RE, b84d02c) — accepted as drafted.** Eleven steps ordered by decisiveness with
mechanical acceptance checks; the checks are ADVERSARIAL where it matters (S5 must reject a
planted nested lattice / capacity-bound sizing / zero-k instance with DISTINCT errors; S7 must
reject exactly the planted label-trivial instance; S9 must find exactly two planted fabrication
variants and classify both). S10 sets no fabrication-rate threshold — the rate goes to the team,
correctly. Study cells, env-2, and deferred items excluded WITH reasons so the gaps read as
decisions, not oversights. Spec-wins precedence stated. RE's cron flag accepted as a MECHANISM,
not a marker: the cron will be built to hard-stop before S10/S11 unless an explicit
authorisation line exists in the backlog — a marker in a document is not a mechanism, so the
check goes in the thing that reads the document.

**v2 verification (reviewer) — all carried numbers verify at source** (seed arithmetic; 0/221
with scope caveat; 2/56; 72.5%; 52-budget arithmetic), with ONE SUPERSEDED: "7 of 9
within-seed-dominated DVs" was true when written but `check_variance.txt` now carries TWELVE
DVs (rerouted_share, any_reroute, time_to_reroute added after §89) and the figure is **10 of
12** — including the allocation family itself (0.587/0.659/0.852), which STRENGTHENS the
agent-free admission justification. Corrected in v2 §7 and BACKLOG S7 with the file-set named.

**The five grid holes (mine — the grid had no adversarial eyes until this pass; the reviewer's
process point stands and is the standing argument for cross-review of every owned artifact):**
- **H1 (BLOCKER, idea-level): the grid was sized by the statistic §4.4 itself demotes.** S=9
  is a sign-test property; under the primary continuous statistic (CHECK-2 priors σ≈0.10–0.15,
  P14-provisional), n=9/cell detects Δ≈0.13–0.20 and supports NO equivalence claim
  (±0.10 needs ~12–28/cell). Our own record (0/864 consumption, 2/56 sends) predicts nulls in
  exactly the single-channel cells — so the design as drawn could not license the
  most-expected finding ("channel X added nothing"). Goes to the researcher as a budget fork
  (options A/B/C in v2 §8; LS recommendation B).
- **H2 (BLOCKER, claim-scope): no unswapped arm existed anywhere in the 45 episodes** — the
  study could say "channels change allocation GIVEN a replacement" but "the replacement
  changed anything" rested on a 2-episode gate that licenses capability only. RULED: cell U
  (unswapped control) is IN, in every budget option. U scores against its own roster's oracle
  (the pre-swap roster persists), so U-vs-0 compares regret against each cell's own attainable
  optimum.
- **H3 (adopted, free): cell 1 could measure RE-READING, not card consumption** — P3 in
  standard form. Fix: log whether the card was rendered into the manager's observation after
  t_swap; report cell 1 conditional on that as a DENOMINATOR, never a stratifier.
- **H4 (adopted): cell 3 conflates availability with use.** Pre-committed rule: report ask
  rate per cell; if ~0, cell 3 is a REACHABILITY result and is reported as such.
- **H5 (adopted): cell 4 relabelled CEILING** — "with everything available, how close to
  oracle?" — a genuinely interesting bound, NOT an interaction claim (cell4 ≈ max vs > sum
  readings are interaction claims the grid disclaims). In budget option A it is cut to fund
  the swap control.
- **Naming (adopted): every contrast is MARGINAL** — behaviour (artifacts, outcomes) is an
  always-present fifth channel in every cell. Licensed claim: "the card added nothing beyond
  what behaviour already showed" — never "the card had no effect". Sentence into v2 §8.

**Verified faithful, unchanged:** triviality ceiling, O3 restatement, three-assertion
detector, admission criterion, attainability-vs-discoverability sentence (to the paper
verbatim). Cross-cell comparisons cleared as clean single-channel contrasts; card-vs-declaration
comparisons are differences of differences, labelled indirect.

*[§135 addendum, 2026-08-07 — researcher ruling on the H1 fork: A/B/C all declined as too
long; "keep things short for quick testing." Adopted: PILOT TIER — cells U/0/ceiling × 3
seeds (9 episodes) + gate pair + fabrication probes ≈ half a day of flash; the
maximum-information contrast (0 vs ceiling) runs as the cheapest decisive test; single-channel
cells and full-grid sizing DEFERRED until pilot variance replaces the P14-provisional priors.
H1's power fact stands for the eventual release. v2 §8 updated.]*
